areas.area: M3 saves — remaining autosave points, the Load/Save screen, and save-format freeze readiness
areas.notes:
BACKLOG.md:110 is accurate on all three of its claims — none of the three is done, and none is even partly started. But the line understates the slice: auditing it turned up four further gaps in the same subsystem, two of which are live defects rather than missing features.

The two live defects:
1. `played_seconds` (M3-SAVE-02) is written into every save header and never incremented anywhere — its own doc comment at GameState.gd:151-153 says "Counted by the router on every screen change" and no router hook exists. Every slot on the Load/Save screen the backlog asks for would read "just started" forever. Fix it before building the screen.
2. `tavern_board` (M3-SAVE-06) is absent from `to_dict()`, and Tavern.gd:89-90 re-rolls the board whenever it is empty — which after any load it always is. That is docs/14 §7.1's `rng_town` row named verbatim ("Otherwise reloading rerolls the recruit list"), it contradicts docs/04 §3.4's "the slot stays empty until the next refresh", and it is a free-reroll exploit: quit to menu, Continue, walk into the Tavern, and the `50g × 2^n` reroll ladder at GameState.gd:1148 is bypassed entirely.

On the attempt-start save (M3-SAVE-03), state the scope honestly when implementing: because `_on_depart` runs the whole sim AND `record_attempt` (which autosaves) inside one synchronous call, alt-F4 mid-RaidView already cannot undo a wipe. The hole that remains is seed-shopping — `next_raid_seed()` keys off the TOTAL attempt count across all encounters, so a reload followed by one unrelated Adventure produces a different seed for the same retry. Persisting the drawn seed in `active_run` is what actually closes it. There is no mid-encounter `sim_state` to serialise today and inventing one would be fabricating a field nothing writes; say so in the comment rather than leaving the §7.1 row looking half-implemented.

On the Load/Save screen's archetype: (C) full-page list/detail per art/ref/specs/10-screen-audit.md §1, built from game/screens/Settings.gd as a template — that file is the project's cleanest C-archetype example (Frame with `tall: true`, dimmed guildhall plate, one warm panel, footer in the sidebar). It works from the title screen as well as in game because `Frame.standard_chips` already degrades to a single "No guild loaded." chip (game/ui/Frame.gd:394-397). docs/13 §5 gives Save/Load no S-number of its own (S01 is "Title / Guild select"), so the in-game entry point is a genuine ambiguity — per the project's rule it goes behind a decision recorded in docs/15, not resolved silently.

Two coordination notes for whoever sequences these: M3-SAVE-03 and M3-SAVE-06 each want a SAVE_VERSION bump 10→11, so land them together or in a stated order; and whichever bump lands first is the opportunity M3-SAVE-07 has been waiting for — `OLDEST_MIGRATABLE` (10) currently equals `SAVE_VERSION` (10), `MIGRATIONS` is `{}`, `tests/data/` is an empty directory, and tests/unit/test_savegame.gd:200-203 contains an explicit early-return acknowledging the chain has never been walked. Commit the v10 fixture BEFORE bumping.

Nothing in this slice is blocked-needs-human. Every item traces to a doc section and every acceptance test can be written headlessly against the existing harness.

areas.area: M3 — Legendary quirks (Q-58) and the five BIG-dumb conditions (Q-59)
areas.notes:
HEADLINE, and it is the one thing to act on first: docs/15 Q-59 and BUILD_STATE.md:246 both claim BIG-dumb condition #1 is "Live — `Raider.consecutive_benched` already counts it exactly". It does not. `grep -rn consecutive_benched --include=*.gd .` finds five hits and not one is a write. `big_dumb_active` is therefore always false in real play, which means the Legendary morale floor of 40 is currently unconditional and canon's "unless you are BIG dumb" escape hatch is unreachable — zero of five conditions are live, not one of five. The same defect hides three more counters: `RaidSim._queue_deltas()` (sim/core/RaidSim.gd:815-822) builds `deltas_queued` and nothing in `game/` ever applies it, so `runs_attended` and `wipes_witnessed` are permanently 0 while game/screens/RaiderDetail.gd:630-632 prints them to the player, and `loot_received` is never incremented either. The `benched` morale trigger (sim/core/Morale.gd:201) is fully specced and never fired. That is Q59-0 and it is the cheapest, highest-value item in the slice.

ON Q-58, LOUDLY: docs/07 does not spec the quirks. `grep -ci quirk docs/07-combat-simulation.md` is 0 — the word appears zero times in the doc that docs/04 §11.2 names as the owner. The BACKLOG line is right and the work is NOT "implement nine effects"; it is "a designer writes nine effects, then implement". Two things make that spec pass harder than it looks: (1) the ownership pointer is broken — docs/04:662 links doc 07 to `07-classes-and-roles.md`, a file that does not exist, and the classes doc is docs/06, so "specced in doc 07" may have meant the classes doc under an older numbering (Q58-2); (2) five of the nine quirks name mechanics the sim does not contain at all — there is no buff/duration system (shaman), no bard ability of any kind and no "phase change" concept (bard, itself double-blocked by docs/06 §5 and docs/07 OQ-10), no mana pool (cleric, blocked on docs/07 OQ-1 which is still unresolved), no in-encounter recovery event (mage), no pre-enrage decision (wizard), and no role-swap (druid). Only warrior, rogue and monk have a hook that exists today (Q58-3). A nice find for the designer: docs/04:397's own Natsuna example already contains a fully-formed quirk — `quirk: chain_heal_never_misses_third_target` — which is expressible against `MIS_CHAIN_FIZZLE` (sim/core/Mistakes.gd:88) and which the shipped data file's "The Totem Holds" silently contradicts.

Q58-4 is the one Q-58 item a build loop can close unblocked: LegendaryPool parses the quirk record and never exposes it (no `quirk_of()`, no validation), so the seam — accessor, validation, a `sim/core/Quirks.gd` registry with four identity-valued hooks behind `ENABLED := false`, proven inert by the goldens' own SHA-256 — can land now and make the eventual spec a data change.

Two smaller things worth recording that fell out of the reads. First, an ordering subtlety that will bite condition #2: `_refresh_big_dumb()` is called only from `_resolve_day_tick()` (game/core/GameState.gd:895), which `record_attempt()` reaches AFTER `_apply_raid_morale()` has already applied the wipe delta — so the third wipe's own hit is still floored and the suspension bites only from the next event. Decide it deliberately or record it. Second, docs/15 has two Q-31s: the upkeep ruling is a summary-table row at line 454, while the section anchored `#q-31` at line 1066 is "Duplicate protection". Q-59's own footnote link at line 1421 therefore points at the wrong question.

One structural observation across both halves: the `flags` dictionary on GameState (docs/14 §5.2's "canon Maybe systems each get a flag") has never been used — `grep -rn 'flags\[' --include=*.gd game sim` is empty. Both the wishlist module (Q59-3) and the quirk seam (Q58-4) are supposed to ship behind flags, so whichever lands first is also building the flag registry; do it once, deliberately, rather than twice with two conventions.

Finally, on scope discipline: condition #5 (Q59-5) is not really a Legendary feature. It is the game's only recurring gold sink, docs/11 never wrote it despite Q-31 assigning it there, and Q-31 and docs/04 §11.3 disagree on whether it is per-run or per-payday. If the designer is unavailable, the correct action is to leave it false and say so — which is exactly what Q-59 already decided, and that decision still holds.

The post-mortem is worse: `game/screens/Results.gd:802` uses `Entry.describe()`, whose MISTAKE branch (EventLog.gd:70-73) is header-only.
- Encounter `comedy_line`: 8 of the 42 docs/16 budgets, all authored and validated (`sim/model/Encounter.gd:202`).

THE BUDGET, from measurement rather than from the doc.
Docs say ≥6 variants per type (docs/07:530 rule 4; docs/14:487; docs/14:536 assertion 7). The shipped goldens say that is not enough for one encounter, let alone one raid. Per-type occurrences inside a SINGLE encounter, counted from `tests/golden/`:
  e5_miserable_commons (16 rounds, 64 mistakes): AFK 13, Wrong Target 11, Heal Wrong 10, Taunt Lapse 9, Aggro 9, Argument 7
  e1_commons_starting (22 rounds, 52 mistakes): Taunt Lapse 12, Aggro 9, Heal Wrong 8, AFK 6, Argument 6
  e5_legendaries_raid (17 rounds): 2 mistakes total — the top of the range is exactly right, which is why legendaries need only ~4 lines each.
docs/15 Q-21 (RESOLVED) records the post-rescale worst sweep cell at 144 mistakes/encounter, ~2.25× e5_miserable_commons, so a hot type can plausibly reach ~29 in one fight.
Recommended: `MIN_VARIANTS = 6` (all 18, the doc floor, validator-enforced) + `HOT_VARIANTS = 14` (one above the measured 13) for eight types — the six measured hot plus MIS_FIRE and MIS_MECHANIC_DROP, which are ungated and high-weight and only absent from the goldens because no Tier 1 encounter drives their mechanic. Total 8×14 + 10×8 = 192 type lines, plus 9×4 = 36 legendary lines. A shuffle-bag per type per encounter, seeded from `rng.derive("mistake_line", 0, 0)`, turns "6 is too few" into "no verbatim repeat below the readable ceiling, and never two identical lines adjacent, ever".

TWO LIVE BUGS FOUND IN THE PRESENTATION PATH (M5-COMEDY-01, M5-COMEDY-06), both of which must land before any line is written:
1. The entry carries the display NAME, not `MIS_*`, so there is nothing to key a template lookup on (`RaidSim.gd:607` passes `ev.type_name`). `Mistakes.MistakeEvent` also lacks docs/07 §5.1's `log_template_id` field.
2. Severity is written as a Name and read as a key: `RaidSim.gd:607` sends `"Severe"`, `LogPlayer.gd:189-195` looks it up in `SEVERITY_KEYS` (lowercase, `Enums.gd:145`) via `keys.find()` (`Enums.gd:490`) and gets -1. So docs/13 §11.2's comedy brake never fires on a real raid, and `RaidView._mistake_header` (RaidView.gd:943) prints `Greg (Rogue) — ? — Pulled Aggro Off the Tank`. The guard at `tests/unit/test_log_player.gd:112` passes only because its fixture hand-writes the lowercase key the sim does not emit.

BACKLOG ACCURACY. `BACKLOG.md:157` ("Mistake log-line writing pass") is accurate as open, but it is under-scoped: it reads as a content task, and roughly half the work here is unbuilt plumbing (template key, loader, renderer, validator, repeat test) plus two live bugs. Suggest replacing the single line with the thirteen items above, and adding M5-COMEDY-06 to the M4/bugs section rather than M5 — it is a defect in shipped code, not content breadth. Nothing in my slice is done-backlog-stale.

DETERMINISM NOTE for the implementer: `Rng.derive` (`sim/core/Rng.gd:205-207`) is a pure function of `master_seed ^ hash64(channel) ^ (round<<32) ^ ordinal` and does NOT consume parent draws, so a `"mistake_line"` channel cannot shift any simulation outcome. Only the log's serialised fields move, i.e. `full_log_sha256` in the five goldens. Land the two golden-churning commits (M5-COMEDY-01, then M5-COMEDY-05) separately so the second one's diff is exactly "192 jokes appeared".

THE ONE THING A LOOP CANNOT CLOSE: M5-COMEDY-12. docs/16 R-3 says outright that nothing in the doc set can prove the comedy lands, and names a human instrument (X1.9's recall interview) plus a dedicated Comedy writer role. The loop can draft all 228 lines and pass every validator; "genuinely funny" needs the same sign-off docs/15 Q-53 is already waiting on for the name pool.

Backlog accuracy for this slice: BACKLOG.md:167-170 is broadly accurate — M6 is genuinely untouched — with three corrections. areas.area: M4 art tail — class glyphs, provision icons, the diff loop, and the remaining placeholders
areas.notes:
Three corrections to the backlog, each proved above: (1) page arrows are DONE and wired (gen_icons.lua:496/501 -> Widgets.gd:165), so BACKLOG.md:133 overstates the gap; (2) of the six provision SKUs three icons are drawn, and — the finding the backlog does not have — NONE of the three is loaded by any screen, so the Market and RaidPrep shelves are pure text; (3) the same is true of the one class glyph that exists: `grep -rn "icons/class" game/` is empty, so `class_warrior.png` has no consumer at all. Per the brief, the honest answer for the glyphs is "wire them", not "drop the item" — the reference measures the glyph on the roster card (01 §3), Concept 3 measures it again (03 §4), and the type spec's `type.class` role is literally defined as "'Warrior' beside the class glyph" (05 §80). So the work splits cleanly into art (m4t-01) and wiring (m4t-02).

On the diff loop: the stored measurements settle the argument that BACKLOG.md:135 only asserts. RaidPrep's chrome-masked IoU is 0.1744 — LOWER than Kit's unmasked 0.2796 and Town's 0.4113. Masking the picture and grading only the typeset chrome makes the score worse, which is only possible if the residual is letterform edges. Whole-screen IoU > 0.65 is therefore unreachable by construction, and more passes against it are wasted iterations. m4t-06 is the fix: per-region scoring with a chrome/text/scene split, edge-IoU kept for chrome and replaced for text by three font-agnostic measures (baseline drift <= 2px, ink-coverage delta <= 0.06, word-run bbox IoU >= 0.80). Every region rect it needs is already measured in specs 01 §1-§4, 02 §0-§8 and 03 §1 — no new measurement work.

On expand mode: the switch ships and applies live (GameSettings.gd:209, Settings.gd:313) but the layout cannot follow it. `Frame.relayout()` is fully size-aware and NOTHING calls it after build — the only `resized` string in game/ is the comment at Frame.gd:248 recommending the handler nobody wrote. So the wide-screen check has to assert four things, in order: the 1536 framing is byte-for-byte the spec's rects (the regression guard), the edge-anchored regions follow a 1820-wide canvas, relayout actually fires on resize, and the 284px band beside the 1536-wide plates is ground colour with no control off-canvas. That last one is exactly what spec 11 §1 says overturned expand as the default.

Two things I did NOT flag as blocked-needs-human, with reasoning: the facility thumbnails (m4t-10) are derivable from the existing plate crop by the same HSV/stamp technique derive_busts.py already uses, so a loop can attempt them — but the item states the eye-test that must fail before it is escalated. The class-glyph silhouette gate in docs/12 §5.1 ("three people name 8 of 9") genuinely is human, and m4t-01 says so rather than pretending the test can be run. One canon ambiguity surfaced and is queued for docs/15 as Q-60 rather than resolved: docs/12 §5.1 makes the shield the Warrior's identifying silhouette while the reference's Warrior glyph is crossed swords, and spec 02 §9.2 has already spent crossed swords on the generic objective glyph.

Provenance gap worth knowing: `class_warrior.png` and `badge_0..6.png` have no generator anywhere in tools/ — they are hand-crops of Concept 1 at the exact spec rects. Both m4t-01 and m4t-09 therefore include regenerating them, so the sets become reproducible rather than one-off artifacts. Separately, `tools/build_art.sh:31` only auto-runs `tools/aseprite/gen_*.lua`, so `tools/art/gen_icons.lua` — which produces most of the icon set — is a manual invocation the pipeline does not cover; m4t-03 asks for that to be closed one way or the other.

THE HEADLINE FINDING. docs/10 §9.1's two HP figures — 350 for Adventure 0 and 1,055 for the Tutorial Raid — are wrong by the same factor and for the same reason that docs/15 Q-28 already corrected for A1-A3. Both are derived from stage A (full Tier 1 Adventure gear, docs/08 §9.1); both tutorials are played at stage 0 (canon starting armour, no weapon, 16.5/round for six per docs/08 §9.1a). The correct figures are 66 and 198. An implementer following this project's normal discipline — transcribe the doc verbatim, never invent a number — will ship two unwinnable tutorials. Q-28's own instruction covers this case ("each rung is sized for the gear the rung before it dropped"), and the correction is a citation of docs/08 §9.1a rather than a locally invented figure, so it is legal under the source rule. The swings (A0 20 raw x1, TR 15 raw x2) are NOT affected — they come from docs/08 §9.3's tank-clock formula and stand unchanged.

RECOMMENDED ORDER: 02 and 13(b) first (they unblock authoring), then 04, 03, 01, 05, 07, 06, 14, 08 — with 09 landing in the same release as 08 or ahead of it. 10, 11 and 12 are independent quality items that make the tutorials teach what they are for; 10 is the largest and touches goldens, so it should not ride with the content commit.

NOTHING IN THIS SLICE IS BLOCKED ON A HUMAN. Every ambiguity found (zero-mechanic A0, tanks 0 vs 1, skip permanence, skip-counts-as-onboarding, the reduced-rate number, and the three-way trinket name/stat fork) has a documented tie-break in docs/09 §10.2, docs/15 Q-47, Q-51, Q-55 or Q-90, so the loop can decide each one by citation and record it, per the project's own rule. PLAYTEST — `tests/unit/test_full_loop.gd` is a genuinely good base to build on (it presses real Buttons via `_press()`/`_must_press()` and was verified as a real gate by cutting a navigation link), but it only ever plays A1. Autoloads are available under `godot --script`, which that file proves at line 44-45, so a campaign driver can use the real `GameState`. The campaign ladder is strictly ordered A1,A2,A3,E1..E5 (`AdventureBoard.gd:444-458`) and reputation gates nothing at Tier 1 (`Reputation.gd` GATES[0] already opens `max_raid_tier: 1`), so "completable" = reach `has_cleared(E5)` from a New Guild. Guild disband cannot fire today (`GameState.gd:117-118` — gated on tutorials that do not exist), so the dead-end path to watch is attrition plus a 60 G floor on the cheapest hire, not disband.

BALANCE — the sweep grid is `SLOTS = E1..E5` only (balance_sweep.gd:25): the Adventure on-ramp A1-A3 has never been swept, and its numbers were last measured by hand in iteration 32. There is no documented target clear-rate curve anywhere in `docs/` — only target *rounds* (docs/08 §9.2) and the 1-to-5-star ramp — so "tune to target clear-rate curve" is asking for a number canon does not publish, and "across all tiers" is asking for content M5 has not written. That item genuinely needs a person; everything else in the balance slice does not.

Two cross-cutting cautions. (1) Every item that starts the engine must go through `tools/with_godot_lock.sh` — its header explains that two concurrent engine invocations corrupt `.godot/` and `user://`, and the symptom is a save test failing in a run that never touched saves. (2) `docs/14` §10.1's gate list and §9.3's sweep spec were both written against a project shape that never materialised (`content_src/`, `gen_items.gd`, `export_all.ps1`, `check_sim_purity.sh`, `tools/sweep.gd`). items.spec_source: docs/07-combat-simulation.md §9 (save-scum policy table, row 1); docs/14-technical-architecture.md §7.1 (`active_run`) and §7.4 (row 3); docs/15 Q-53 (DECIDED)
items.risk: The real hole this closes is narrower than the backlog implies and should be stated honestly in the commit: because the whole sim resolves synchronously in `_on_depart` and `record_attempt` autosaves immediately, alt-F4 mid-RaidView already cannot undo a wipe. Delete presses `SaveGame.erase_slot(row["slot"])` (SaveGame.gd:352, removes the manual save, all 3 autosaves and their `.bak`s) behind a confirm; rebuild the rows after any of the three.

items.title: "Quit to menu" is the unwired half of docs/14 §7.4's last row — only window close saves
items.evidence: docs/14 §7.4's last row is "Quit to menu / window close | manual-equivalent". Only window close is wired: game/core/GameState.gd:237-243 handles `NOTIFICATION_WM_CLOSE_REQUEST` and calls `save_now()` before `quit()`. The two quit-to-menu paths call neither: game/screens/Town.gd:236-238 `_on_back()` is bare `_router.goto(MAIN_MENU)`, and game/screens/Settings.gd:420-425 `_on_back()` saves only `GameSettings` (`_save()` → `_settings.save_to_disk()`) before falling through to `goto(MAIN_MENU)` when the stack is one deep. Neither path calls `_state.save_now()` or `_state.reset()`, so everything since the last of the three autosave triggers is silently dropped when the player then presses Continue.

items.risk: `migrate()` (SaveGame.gd:224-231) deliberately RETURNS THE BODY UNCHANGED when a version has no registered step, on the reasoning that from_dict defaults are honest. items.title: Leg 3 is the missing one — no town building is rank-gated on the town screen, and the Blacksmith has no ladder at all
items.evidence:
VERIFIED AGAINST THE TREE 2026-09-11 — THE EVIDENCE BELOW IS STALE. (reconciliation sweep: one agent read this entry and the files it names, and every claim of 'done' was then put to two independent skeptics whose brief was to refute it. Four survived the read and did not survive the refutation.)
Specifically no longer true: "sim/core/Buildings.gd:26-50 LADDERS has guildhall/tavern/market/board and NO blacksmith key"
What the tree actually shows now:
  - sim/core/Buildings.gd:32 LADDERS now HAS a "blacksmith" key (rows at :48-62) with docs/02 §11's three rungs verbatim: {"level":1,"rank":2,"cost":300}, {2,3,700}, {3,4,1600} — the audit's "NO blacksmith key" is false. The class docstring at :26-30 was also rewritten to say why "level 1 is always present" no longer holds.
  - sim/core/Buildings.gd:96 base_level() returns 0 for the blacksmith and 1 for everything else; sim/core/Buildings.gd:186 defines entry_blocker(building, gold, rank) -> String, which short-circuits to "" when base_level>0 and otherwise delegates to upgrade_blocker(building, 0, gold, rank) so the rank-then-price wording is not duplicated.
  - CALLER VERIFIED, not just the definition: game/screens/Town.gd:310 _unlock_reason() calls Buildings.entry_blocker(String(b["id"]), _state.gold, _state.reputation_rank) between the feature-flag check and the _router.screen_exists check — the third gate the audit says does not exist. Gate order (flag, then rank/price, then missing scene) is documented at Town.gd:293-299.
  - CALLER VERIFIED for the §7 town column: game/screens/Town.gd:220 _sidebar() adds Widgets.label_as(_town_unlock_line(), "LabelSmall"); _town_unlock_line() at Town.gd:265 calls Reputation.town_unlock(rank) at :271 and Reputation.town_unlock(rank + 1) at :273, clamping at the top via Reputation.rp_for_next(rank) < 0. town_unlock() now lives at sim/core/Reputation.gd:617 reading data/reputation.json's per-rank "town_unlock" rows (Known = "Guildhall facility upgrade I; Quest board", Respected = "Blacksmith opens").
  - Tests exist for all of it. tests/unit/test_screens.gd: test_the_smithy_names_the_rank_that_opens_it asserts "Reach Respected" at rank UNKNOWN with flags["blacksmith"]=true; test_a_respected_guild_is_quoted_the_smithys_price_instead asserts "Costs 300 G" and the absence of "Reach Respected"; test_a_flagged_off_smithy_is_absent_rather_than_rank_locked pins the flag-before-rank order; test_a_met_rank_stops_taking_the_blame_for_a_missing_screen asserts the fall-through to "Not built in this version yet."; test_a_shut_door_is_a_disabled_button_whose_reason_is_printed finds the disabled "Blacksmith" Button and its Label reason; test_the_town_says_what_the_next_rank_opens asserts "Next at Known" + "Quest board"; test_a_legendary_guild_is_not_promised_a_seventh_rank pins the clamp.
  - tests/unit/test_buildings.gd is new (187 lines, added in commit 4a5b09a) and covers the ladder rows (:20-49), base_level("blacksmith")==0 (:54-66), entry_blocker's rank sentence and price sentence (:70-91), reputation_level("blacksmith", LEGENDARY)==0 (:134-135), and the base_level/first-rung invariant (:162-169).
  - THE HOLE: `grep -rn blacksmith_tier` over the whole tree returns nothing. game/core/GameState.gd:317-318 declares only tavern_tier and market_tier; building_level() at GameState.gd:2040 matches "guildhall"/"tavern"/"market" and falls through to `_: return 1`, so GameState.building_level("blacksmith") answers 1 while Buildings.base_level("blacksmith") is 0 — the two modules now disagree. The save dict at GameState.gd:2541-2542 and the loader at :2647-2648 carry no blacksmith key. git show --stat 4a5b09a ("the macro loop's third leg: the town finally reads the rank") touched only Town.gd, Buildings.gd, test_buildings.gd and test_screens.gd — GameState.gd was never opened.
  - The gap is latent, not live: the only callers of upgrade_building() are game/screens/Market.gd:296 ("market") and game/screens/Tavern.gd:559 ("tavern"), and there is still no game/screens/Blacksmith.gd or .tscn, so nothing asks GameState for a blacksmith level today. Nothing in tests/unit/ asserts building_level("blacksmith").
  - The design question the item flagged was recorded rather than silently resolved: build/plan/q-town-loop.md holds a proposed docs/15 BL entry ruling that the §11 rows ship but the Q8 decision stays behind the `blacksmith` flag, and that Q8's alternate reading (moving the Tavern's L4 rung down) is deliberately not implemented. sim/core/Buildings.gd:61 cites that file.

ORIGINAL EVIDENCE, kept as the record of why this was filed:
game/screens/Town.gd:225-233 `_unlock_reason()` has exactly two gates and neither is reputation: the canon-Maybe feature flag, and whether the scene exists. The Blacksmith entry (Town.gd:58-63) carries `"flag": "blacksmith"` and nothing else, so at Legendary rank it still reads "Canon lists this one as a maybe. Disabled in this build." sim/core/Buildings.gd:26-50 LADDERS has guildhall/tavern/market/board and NO blacksmith key, although docs/02 §11 prices it (L1 Respected 300 G, L2 Established 700 G, L3 Renowned 1600 G) and docs/03 §7 makes "Blacksmith opens" the entire town unlock for Respected. Rank gating that DOES work is upgrade-only and lives off the town screen: Buildings.upgrade_blocker (Buildings.gd:87-99) checks rank first then price, called from game/core/GameState.gd:1107, surfaced on game/screens/Market.gd:278 and game/screens/Tavern.gd:462. And the §7 town column is dead copy: `grep -rn "town_unlock\|market_stock"` finds definitions at sim/core/Reputation.gd:357,361 and ONE caller — tests/unit/test_reputation.gd:498-504 — so no screen has ever printed what a rank opens in town.
items.remaining_work:
VERIFIED AGAINST THE TREE 2026-09-11 — WHAT IS ACTUALLY LEFT:
Edit (2) of remaining_work is the only piece missing, and it was never started: GameState has no `blacksmith_tier`, no `"blacksmith"` case in `building_level()` (GameState.gd:2040), and no blacksmith key in the save/load pair (GameState.gd:2541-2542 / :2647-2648). Two concrete consequences. (a) `GameState.building_level("blacksmith")` returns 1 via the `_` fallback, contradicting `Buildings.base_level("blacksmith") == 0`; `upgrade_building("blacksmith")` (GameState.gd:2053) would therefore read level 1, quote the L2 rung (700 G at Renowned) instead of the 300 G L1 purchase, and increment nothing, so the smithy can never actually be bought or persisted. (b) Because no purchase state exists, the town's gate is an affordability check rather than a "have you bought it" check — test_screens.gd's test_a_met_rank_stops_taking_the_blame_for_a_missing_screen pins exactly that: a Respected guild holding 999 G passes the gate having paid nothing. Neither is reachable today (no Blacksmith screen, and upgrade_building is only ever called with "market"/"tavern"), and nothing tests building_level("blacksmith"). Everything else in the item — the ladder, base_level, entry_blocker, the Town gate ordering, the printed §7 town-unlock line, and every acceptance assertion named in remaining_work — is in the tree and tested.

THE ORIGINAL PLAN, kept for the HOW — some of its clauses are already met, see above for which:
Three edits plus a structural wrinkle. (1) Add a `"blacksmith"` ladder to sim/core/Buildings.gd with docs/02 §11's rungs. Note the wrinkle: Buildings.gd:22 states "Level 1 is always present at the start and always free", which is true of the other four buildings and false of the Blacksmith, whose L1 itself costs 300 G at Respected — so the blacksmith ladder needs a `{"level": 1, "rank": 2, "cost": 300}` rung and `building_level("blacksmith")` must be able to return 0. Update that docstring rather than leaving it lying. (2) Add `blacksmith_tier: int = 0` to game/core/GameState.gd beside tavern_tier/market_tier (declared near :80, reset near :262, serialised at :1540, loaded at :1613-1614) and a `"blacksmith"` case in `building_level()` (:1090-1099). (3) Give sim/core/Buildings.gd an `entry_blocker(building, level, gold, rank) -> String` sibling to `upgrade_blocker` that returns the rank sentence for a building not yet standing, and call it from Town.gd `_unlock_reason()` BEFORE the flag and scene checks so a rank-locked building says which rank opens it. (4) Print the town half of docs/03 §7: in Town.gd's sidebar next to the existing blurb at :188-193 ("Reputation decides what appears here. Raids raise reputation.") add a Label carrying `Reputation.town_unlock(rank + 1)` so the §7 column stops being computed-and-never-shown. Acceptance: extend tests/unit/test_screens.gd:289 `test_unbuilt_buildings_are_disabled_with_a_reason_not_hidden` with a rank case — with `flags["blacksmith"] = true` and rank Unknown the Town's collected Label text contains "Reach Respected"; at Respected it contains "300 G" instead; and a new assertion that the sidebar names what the next rank opens. Keep every one of these strings in Labels and Buttons — the screen tests walk only `Label.text` and `Button.text`.
items.risk: There is no Blacksmith screen — `ls game/screens/` has no Blacksmith.gd or .tscn — so even with the flag on and the rank met, `_unlock_reason()` falls through to "Not built in this version yet." The rank gate must therefore be asserted at the Buildings level and through the printed string, never by navigating to the screen. Also docs/03 §11 Q8 is still open on whether the Blacksmith is rank-gated at all ("if cut, Respected instead unlocks the Tavern expansion, moved down from Renowned") — implement the gate behind the existing `blacksmith` feature flag, which is what docs/14 §5.2's "completable with every flag off" rule already requires, and do not move the Tavern rung.

items.title: The Adventure's Board's levels are dead data — the ladder exists, nothing advances it, nothing reads it
items.evidence:
VERIFIED AGAINST THE TREE 2026-09-11 — THE EVIDENCE BELOW IS STALE. (reconciliation sweep: one agent read this entry and the files it names, and every claim of 'done' was then put to two independent skeptics whose brief was to refute it. Four survived the read and did not survive the refutation.)
Specifically no longer true: "tests/unit/test_tavern.gd:154 asserts every board rung is free, which is the only thing that touches them."
What the tree actually shows now:
  - sim/core/Buildings.gd:66-73 still defines the board ladder (L2 rank 1 cost 0, L3 rank 2 cost 0) with the 'Free: it upgrades by reputation, not gold' note — unchanged, but it is no longer dead data at the sim layer.
  - sim/core/Buildings.gd:126 defines `reputation_level(building, rank)` — the derivation the item asks for (base_level, then max rung whose "rank" <= rank, and it refuses to derive a priced ladder).
  - sim/core/Buildings.gd:109 defines `is_reputation_only(building)` — docs/14 §5.3.7's 'gold_cost == 0 for every Board level' validator, asked as a predicate.
  - sim/core/Buildings.gd:198 defines `purchase_refusal(building, level)` returning 'Reputation opens this, not gold. Reach %s.' / '...and there is nothing left to open.' — the gold refusal the item asks for, but at the Buildings layer, not GameState's.
  - game/screens/Town.gd:242-247 is the only production caller: `if Buildings.is_reputation_only(id)` then prints 'Level %d of %d' from `Buildings.reputation_level(id, _state.reputation_rank)` — so the derived level IS read by a screen.
  - tests/unit/test_buildings.gd:109 `test_the_boards_level_is_the_rank_and_nothing_else` asserts `reputation_level("board", rank)` == [1,2,3,3,3,3] across all six ranks — exactly the item's 1/2/3/3 acceptance vector; :118 asserts monotonicity; :129 asserts a priced ladder cannot be derived.
  - tests/unit/test_buildings.gd:98 asserts `is_reputation_only("board")` and false for the other four; :148 `test_gold_can_never_buy_a_board_rung` asserts `purchase_refusal("board",1)` contains 'not gold' and 'Reach Known', and :153 the top-of-ladder wording.
  - UNARMED SEAM 1 — game/core/GameState.gd:2040 `building_level()` still matches only "guildhall"/"tavern"/"market" and falls through `_: return 1`. There is no "board" case and nothing in GameState calls `Buildings.reputation_level` (grep for `reputation_level` hits only Buildings.gd:126 and Town.gd:245). `GameState.building_level("board")` is 1 at every rank.
  - UNARMED SEAM 2 — game/core/GameState.gd:2054 `upgrade_building()` never calls `purchase_refusal`; it asks `Buildings.upgrade_blocker(building, level, gold, rank)` (Buildings.gd:159), which at cost 0 passes the price gate. At Known+ `upgrade_building("board")` returns "" — a silent successful no-op (the `match` at :2066 has no "board" branch) — which is precisely the hole tests/unit/test_buildings.gd:140 `test_a_price_check_cannot_refuse_a_free_rung` documents as still open.
  - No test anywhere touches `GameState.building_level` or `GameState.upgrade_building("board")`: `grep -rn building_level --include=*.gd .` returns only game/core/GameState.gd:2040 and :2055; `upgrade_building` callers are game/screens/Market.gd:296, game/screens/Tavern.gd:559, tests/unit/test_tavern.gd:192 — all hard-coded to "market"/"tavern".

ORIGINAL EVIDENCE, kept as the record of why this was filed:
sim/core/Buildings.gd:42-49 defines board rungs at level 2 (rank 1) and level 3 (rank 2), both cost 0, with the comment "Free: it upgrades by reputation, not gold". But game/core/GameState.gd:1090-1099 `building_level()` has no `"board"` case, so it hits the `_:` default and returns 1 forever; `upgrade_building` has no board caller (`grep -rn "upgrade_building"` finds only game/screens/Market.gd:287, game/screens/Tavern.gd:467, tests/unit/test_tavern.gd:192). tests/unit/test_tavern.gd:154 asserts every board rung is free, which is the only thing that touches them. docs/14:518 says the validator must assert `gold_cost == 0` for every Board level — there is nothing for it to validate, and docs/02 §9.2 gives the Board three exterior deltas keyed to levels that can never change.

items.title: docs/02 §9's rank → visible town change has no mechanism at all — the camp scene is the same at Unknown and at Legendary
items.evidence: `grep -rn "scene_flags\|npc_pool\|time_of_day" --include=*.gd .` returns nothing — docs/02 §3.2's three town-state fields are unimplemented. game/assets/scenes/camp.json contains a static plate plus three props and three lights with no conditional key of any kind (`grep -c rank` on both scene files returns 0), and game/ui/SceneStage.gd `_build()` (:78) instantiates all of them unconditionally. game/screens/Town.gd:112-130 loads the stage and only swaps the speech-bubble lines. So docs/02 §2.1's acceptance criteria R2 ("every reputation rank adds ≥3 scene deltas") and R5 ("the player can always tell rank from a single screenshot of the town, with no HUD") are both unmet, and canon's "Reputation determines what starts appearing around town" (quoted at docs/03:65) is satisfied only in menus.
items.remaining_work: Build the mechanism, which is data-shaped and cheap. (1) Add optional `"rank_min": int` and `"level_min": {"building": String, "level": int}` keys to each entry of the `props` and `lights` arrays in game/assets/scenes/camp.json (and guildhall.json). (2) In game/ui/SceneStage.gd `_build()` (:78), skip any entry whose gate the current state does not meet; give `SceneStage.load(name)` an optional state argument so the tools/shot.gd fixture path can force a rank without a GameState (tools/shot.gd already seeds fixtures, so keep that seam explicit rather than reaching for the autoload inside `_build`). (3) Add `GameState.scene_flags() -> Array` derived from `reputation_rank` and the building levels, NOT stored — docs/02 §3.2's derivation rule says services and derived state are recomputed at load "so a design retune from invalidating saves". (4) Populate camp.json's gates from docs/02 §9.1's six rows using whatever the existing prop set can express (lit torches, campfire, light energy, bubble density). Acceptance: a headless test that builds the camp stage at each rank 0-5 and asserts the visible-layer count is non-decreasing and that at least one gate fires per rank step; plus an assertion that Town's collected Label/Button strings are IDENTICAL across all six ranks except the rank chip, because the screen-test contract only sees text and these deltas must be visual.
items.risk: The mechanism lands; the fidelity does not. The current camp set is one plate (game/assets/bg/camp_plate.png), two torch strips, one campfire and three lights — nowhere near docs/02 §9.1's crowd counts of 3→26, banners, façade swaps and time-of-day. Expect R2's "≥3 deltas per rank" to be met thinly and R5 ("tell rank from a screenshot") to be missed until M3-LOOP-06 is answered. Do not let that stop the mechanism shipping — a data-gated scene layer is the thing that makes the art cheap when it arrives.

items.title: The six authored town rank-states docs/02 §9.1 asks for cannot be produced by the build loop
items.evidence: docs/02 §9.1 specifies six distinct town states (Unknown: "Guildhall boarded ... 3 idle townsfolk, all turned away" → Legendary: "Statue of the guild in the square ... 26 townsfolk, crowd gathers ... stained glass and a tower"), and §2.1 R5 makes them a hard acceptance criterion. The town has exactly one plate: game/assets/bg/camp_plate.png, cut from the lead designer's reference concept. The user's standing rule (recorded in memory, 2026-09-10) is that the reference concepts set the art bar and the design wins only where their UI does not fit — which means five more plates at that bar, not five generated approximations. Compounding it, docs/03 §5.4 calls the Established gap "THE LARGEST HOLE IN THIS DOC" and says it "needs the lead designer's sign-off"; docs/15:445 (Q-22) carries a recommendation for Established's town content, not a designer ruling.
items.remaining_work: A person must do three things, in this order. (1) Rule on docs/02 §12 Q2 / docs/15 Q-22: does Established carry Market L4 + Blacksmith L2 as its town content, and does docs/03 §5.4's recruit gap-fill stand? Until that is signed, two of the six rank-states have no agreed content to draw. (2) Decide whether §9.1's six states survive for v1 or collapse — the cheap collapse is three visible states (Unknown / Respected / Renowned) with the other three ranks expressed as additive props on the nearest plate, which M3-LOOP-05's gating mechanism already supports without new plates. (3) Supply or commission the plate variants (or the additive prop layers) for whichever set survives. Once (1) and (2) are answered, the build loop can finish the rest without help: the gates are data, and tools/art/refdiff.py plus tools/shot.gd --fixture can score each rank state against its reference the same way the eleven finished screens were scored.
items.risk: This is the one place where the macro loop's canon promise ("the town itself your progression engine", docs/02 §2) is asset-bound rather than code-bound. Recording it as blocked is better than an autonomous pass inventing five town states, which would violate both the reference-concepts standard and the canon-source rule.

items.title: Wire the mechanic-check roll site (docs/07 §5.3b) — it is never rolled, and five mistake types are unreachable
items.evidence: grep -n RollSite sim/core/RaidSim.gd returns exactly four hits: RollSite.ACTION at RaidSim.gd:432 and :482, RollSite.AMBIENT at :564 and :778. Nothing ever sets ctx.roll_site = Enums.RollSite.MECHANIC. Mistakes.eligible_types() hard-filters on site (sim/core/Mistakes.gd:216 `if int(t["site"]) != ctx.roll_site: continue`), so the five MECHANIC-site types are permanently ineligible in a real run: MIS_FIRE (Mistakes.gd:44), MIS_INTERRUPT_MISS (:61), MIS_INTERRUPT_WRONG (:68), MIS_MECHANIC_DROP (:99), MIS_AVOIDABLE_DEATH (:145). Consequences: Token.FIRE is emitted by nothing (only Mistakes.gd:48 and :103 emit it, both MECHANIC-site), so RaidSim.gd:551 `if c.is_alive() and c.has_token(Enums.Token.FIRE)` can never be true; the `"MIS_AVOIDABLE_DEATH"` branch at RaidSim.gd:620 is dead; ctx.interrupt_check (RaidSim.gd:665) gates two types that cannot fire. Formulas.ROLL_SITE_WEIGHT[1] = 0.55 (Formulas.gd:407) was tuned in the Q-21 sweep for a channel nothing uses. BUILD_STATE.md:306 and :308 claim 'mistake rolls at all three sites' / 'three roll sites' — stale.

items.title: M02 Raid-Wide is implemented but mitigated by AC twice — the pulse is supposed to bypass armour
items.evidence: RaidSim.gd:307-315 implements M02: fires when round_no % params.every == 0, computes dmg via Formulas.raid_wide_damage() and applies it per living raider. Formulas.raid_wide_damage (Formulas.gd:64-67) is docstring'd 'Raid-wide and spell damage bypass armour (docs/10 §5.4)' and returns the raw number unchanged — but RaidSim.gd:315 then hands that number to _apply_damage (RaidSim.gd:590), which calls Formulas.damage_after_ac(float(raw), int(p["ac"])) at :593. So the pulse IS reduced by AC. The data says otherwise: data/encounters_t1.json:53, :74, :116 all carry "ignores_ac": true, and tests/unit/test_encounters.gd:127 asserts that flag with the comment 'docs/10 §5.4 assumes raid-wide damage ignores AC so pressure lands on healers'. The params key `ignores_ac` is read nowhere in sim/ (grep: only data files and test_encounters.gd).
items.spec_source: docs/10 §10 M02 ('ignores AC'); docs/10 §5.4; docs/08 §9.5 AOE_BITE_FRACTION 0.35
items.risk: Raises real healer pressure across every encounter that carries m02 (E2, E3, E5, adventure A2/A3). Expect clear rates to drop; check against the balance sweep before accepting the new goldens.

items.title: M04 Add Spawns double-spawns: the m04 mechanic and the authored spawn_round enemy block both fire on the same round
items.evidence: Two independent spawn paths exist and both run at Phase 0. _spawn_scheduled (RaidSim.gd:296-301) activates any EnemyBlock whose spawn_round matches; _apply_scheduled_mechanics's ADD_SPAWNS branch (RaidSim.gd:323-342) appends brand-new Enemy objects. The Tier 1 data configures both for the same round: data/encounters_t1.json:29-30 gives E1 a 'Late Add' block with spawn_round 5 AND :32 an m04 spec with round 5 count 1 — round 5 produces two adds, not one. E2: four 'Add' blocks at spawn_round 4 (:50-51) plus m04 count 2 round 4 every 4 (:52) — round 4 produces six adds, and rounds 8/12/16 add two more each on top of a block that has already fired. E3: three 'Add' blocks at spawn_round 6 (:70-71) plus m04 count 3 round 6 (:75) — six adds. Only E5 is consistent (no authored add blocks; m04 rounds [10,20], :118). The existing test does not catch it — tests/unit/test_raid_sim.gd:238 only asserts the string 'joins the fight' appears, with an `or res.rounds < 5` escape hatch.
items.spec_source: docs/10 §10 M04 ('`count` adds of `hp`/`swing` on round `R`, repeating every `N`'); docs/10 §7 split rule 2 ('Add damage sits on top of that budget')
items.risk: E2 currently accumulates two extra adds every four rounds forever and they are never focused (see m5-add-target-priority), so this bug and that one compound. Fixing one without the other will swing clear rates hard in opposite directions.

items.title: Adds are never focused: raider targeting returns the first enemy in array order, so m04 adds are only attacked after the boss dies
items.evidence: _pick_enemy (RaidSim.gd:729-733) returns the first active, living enemy in `enemies` array order. _build_enemies (RaidSim.gd:214-227) appends in data order (boss first for E3/E4/E5) and the m04 branch appends new adds at the END (RaidSim.gd:340). So while the boss lives, no raider ever swings at an add. Meanwhile adds use threat_rule 'lowest_hp' (RaidSim.gd:339) and _pick_enemy_target (:355-360) makes them hunt the weakest raider every round, unopposed. Victory still requires _living_enemies(enemies) == 0 (RaidSim.gd:787), so adds are killed — last, after the boss. This makes M04 pure unavoidable attrition rather than the DPS-priority test docs/10 says it is, and it hollows out MIS_WRONG_TARGET ('Attacked the Wrong Target … priority target unharmed this round', docs/07 §5.2 row 11) which presupposes a priority target the sim does not model.
items.remaining_work: Give _pick_enemy a priority rule instead of array order. Minimum viable: sort candidates by (is_add desc, current hp asc) — i.e. living adds first, lowest HP first — so DPS clear adds and then return to the boss, matching docs/10 M04's 'adds exist to pressure healers' framing (docs/10 §7 split rule 2) while still letting the boss be the fight. Tag adds explicitly: add `var is_add: bool = false` to the RaidSim.Enemy class (RaidSim.gd:45-57) and set it true in the m04 branch and in the MIS_BROKE_CC/MIS_FACEPULL 'Loose Add' branch (RaidSim.gd:625-631). Then make MIS_WRONG_TARGET mean something: in _apply_mistake, when a DPS rolls it, redirect that raider's damage to a non-priority enemy this round (the boss when adds are up), and log it. Because target priority is a rule and not a coefficient, put the sort behind a named constant (e.g. `const ADD_PRIORITY := true`) and record the ambiguity in docs/15 — docs/10 never states an explicit kill order. Acceptance: a test in tests/unit/test_raid_sim.gd that after an m04 spawn the next DPS ATTACK log entry names the add, and that the encounter's total rounds do not increase for a strong roster (adds should be a detour, not a wall).
items.spec_source: docs/10 §10 M04; docs/10 §7 split rule 2; docs/07 §5.2 row 11 (MIS_WRONG_TARGET); docs/07 §6 Adds token row
items.risk: Silently resolving a kill order would violate the project's canon rule; the switch + docs/15 entry is mandatory, not optional.

items.title: M03 Avoidable Ground Effect is a stub: the tick loop exists but nothing ever puts a raider in the fire, and escape_chance_bp is unread
items.evidence: The only M03 code is RaidSim._phase_effects (RaidSim.gd:546-553): it skips any spec that is not GROUND_EFFECT, then damages any living combatant holding Enums.Token.FIRE. No combatant can hold that token — FIRE is emitted only by MIS_FIRE (Mistakes.gd:48) and MIS_MECHANIC_DROP (Mistakes.gd:103), both RollSite.MECHANIC, a site RaidSim never rolls (see m5-mech-roll-site). There is no entry code into the zone at all: nothing calls Combatant.add_token(Enums.Token.FIRE, ...) — the only add_token call in sim/ is RaidSim.gd:615, which replays ev.tokens_emitted. The authored param `escape_chance_bp` (data/encounters_t1.json:93, :117) is read nowhere; docs/10 M03 requires 'a raider re-rolls out at `p` per round' and docs/07 §5.2 row 1 requires 'leaves at end of next round'. No test exercises m03: grep GROUND_EFFECT in tests/ returns nothing.
items.spec_source: docs/10 §10 M03 ('`X`/round to raiders flagged in-zone; a raider re-rolls out at `p` per round'); docs/07 §5.2 row 1; docs/07 §6 Fire token row
items.risk: M03 is also the gate on MIS_AVOIDABLE_DEATH, the only cascade-only type in the taxonomy (tests/unit/test_mistakes.gd:35 asserts there is exactly one). Until m03 works, the cascade system's terminal event cannot happen in a real fight.

items.title: M05 Interrupt Check is a stub: it sets one context flag and has no cast, no position test and no effect
items.evidence: The sole reference to INTERRUPT_CHECK in sim/ is RaidSim.gd:665, `ctx.interrupt_check = encounter.has_mechanic(Enums.Mechanic.INTERRUPT_CHECK)`, inside _context(). That flag gates only MIS_INTERRUPT_MISS and MIS_INTERRUPT_WRONG (Mistakes.gd:61-74, `"requires": "interrupt_check"`), and both are RollSite.MECHANIC, so neither can be selected at the ACTION site where _context() is used (see m5-mech-roll-site). There is no boss cast, no check that a melee DPS is present, and no effect E. The authored params are unread: data/encounters_t1.json:94 carries {"round": 4, "every": 5, "requires_melee": 1} and nothing in sim/ reads `requires_melee`. _apply_scheduled_mechanics's match (RaidSim.gd:306) has no INTERRUPT_CHECK arm. No test: grep INTERRUPT_CHECK in tests/ returns nothing.

items.title: M10 Mana Burn is absent, and half of it has no resource to burn — the Focus pool from docs/15 Q-02 was never built
items.evidence: grep MANA_BURN outside docs/ returns only sim/model/Enums.gd:232 and Enums.gd:261. No RaidSim branch. The resource half is missing too: Formulas.gd:76-78 declares `enum ManaModel { MAGNITUDE_PLUS_FOCUS, ... }` and `const MANA_MODEL := ManaModel.MAGNITUDE_PLUS_FOCUS`, whose docstring (Formulas.gd:72-75) says 'Focus is a separate class-fixed resource that never appears on an item' — but grep for Focus/focus across sim/ returns only those three comment/const lines. No Combatant field, no pool, no spend. Mana in the sim is a flat magnitude read off the gear profile (RaidSim.gd:186, `"mana": stats.mana + mana_bonus`) and consumed by nothing. The Token.MANA emitted by the three wasted-heal mistakes (Mistakes.gd:80, :86, :92) likewise has no effect: _situational_bp (RaidSim.gd:723-730) only reads AGGRO and DISTRACTION.
items.remaining_work: Split into two shippable halves and say so in docs/15. (a) SHIPPABLE NOW — the silence half. Add a MANA_BURN arm to _apply_scheduled_mechanics that, for params.rounds, marks casters and healers (role_group CASTER/SUPPORT/HEALER off the cached profile, RaidSim.gd:196) as unable to act; enforce it in Combatant.can_act (sim/model/Combatant.gd:82) via a new `silenced_until` field, so _phase_actors (RaidSim.gd:391-398) and _phase_healers (RaidSim.gd:472-494) both honour it with no other change. Emit a STORY line. (b) BLOCKED ON A POOL — the drain half ('casters lose `X` Mana per round'). Build the Focus pool first: `var focus: int` and `var focus_max: int` on Combatant, class-fixed values in data/classes*.json read by sim/model/ClassDef.gd, a spend in _take_action/_cast_heal, and a rule for what a caster does at zero. That is a subsystem, not a mechanic — split it out as its own item before attempting (b). Ship (a) behind `const MANA_BURN_DRAIN_ENABLED := false` and record the split in docs/15 as an entry citing Q-02's Model A+, so the ambiguity is behind a switch rather than resolved silently. Acceptance for (a): a synthetic m10 encounter test asserting no HEAL or spell ATTACK entries from casters during the window, and normal output the round after.

items.title: docs/07 §6 token effects and cascade attribution are not wired — mechanics cannot invite the mistakes they are supposed to
items.evidence: Three divergences from docs/07 §6's table. (1) Mistakes.attribute() (sim/core/Mistakes.gd:354) is never called outside tests — grep 'attribute(' over sim/ and game/ returns only the definition; tests/unit/test_mistakes.gd:306 and :322 call it directly. So in every real sim run ev.caused_by is "" and ev.cascade_depth is 0, and the post-mortem graph docs/07 §6 calls 'this doc's contract' is empty. RaidSim._log_mistake (RaidSim.gd:606) dutifully writes both fields (EventLog.emit_mistake) and they are always blank. (2) The Aggro token is applied to the wrong raider: docs/07 §6 says Aggro gives 'Healers' mistake chance +8pp', but _situational_bp (RaidSim.gd:723-730) adds 800bp to whoever HOLDS the token — the DPS who pulled it. (3) Distraction is documented as '+5pp ambient mistake chance, raid-wide'; the code adds 500bp to the holder only, at every roll site (RaidSim.gd:727-728). The Fire, Mana and Adds rows have no implementation at all: _situational_bp reads only AGGRO and DISTRACTION, so 'wasted heal makes the next heal weaker' and 'Adds add mechanic checks, so every raider rolls more often — this is the main difficulty amplifier' are both absent.
items.remaining_work: (1) Cascade: in RaidSim, when a mistake fires on an actor holding a live token, look up the event that emitted that token and call Mistakes.attribute(ev, parent). This needs a per-encounter map from (combatant, token) -> the MistakeEvent that emitted it — add it to the token bookkeeping in Combatant.add_token (sim/model/Combatant.gd:163) as a parallel `token_sources: Dictionary` (token -> event id string), populated from RaidSim.gd:615's loop which already has both the event and the actor. Then assert in a test that a real sim run of t1_raid_e5 with a miserable Common roster produces at least one entry with a non-empty caused_by. (2) Rewrite _situational_bp to take the ROLLER and the RAID, not just the holder: Aggro live anywhere in the raid adds +800bp to healers' rolls; Distraction live anywhere adds +500bp raid-wide but only at RollSite.AMBIENT; keep the Formulas.SITUATIONAL_CAP_BP = 2000 clamp (Formulas.gd:377). (3) Adds token: implement the amplifier by making the number of mechanic checks per round scale with living adds once the mechanic-check phase exists. Every change here moves mistake volume, so re-measure against docs/15 Q-21's band and update the entry.
items.spec_source: docs/07 §6 (token table + rules 1-4, and the worked cascade); docs/07 §5.2; docs/15 Q-21
items.risk: This is what makes a mechanic 'invite' a mistake rather than merely coexist with one. Without it the answer to 'does each implemented mechanic invite the mistakes docs/07 says it should' is no for all twelve, regardless of how many arms get added to the match statement.

The subtle one, and the reason the file deserved a test at all: conditions that can only be decided while an attempt is being recorded (flawless clear, full-party clear) must answer 'not now' rather than 'no' against a bare snapshot, with the earned set carrying them across a reload. If they answered yes, every reload would hand out every event achievement; if the earned set forgot, a reload would take them away. Both directions are asserted.

items.remaining_work: A person must add the rate to docs/03 §6 (a board-award row and the ~15%-of-RP-earned cap), or say no and make the board coin-and-goods only. Until then the autonomous action is the project's own rule: implement the RP reward kind behind a flag — add `"achievement_rp"` to `GameState.flags`, default FALSE, so `Achievements.claim()` skips RP rewards and the record's reward falls back to its coin equivalent; record the switch and the reason in docs/15 as a new build-loop entry pointing at Q-69. items.spec_source: docs/11 §11.2 ("Total coin from the board across the whole game is capped at ~15% of lifetime income"); docs/16 W3.7 ("hard-capped at ~15% of lifetime income so it can never substitute for playing content"); docs/15 Q-69 (RP capped at ~15% of total earned)
items.evidence: `grep -rn "lifetime|total_earned|gold_earned" game/ sim/` returns one unrelated hit (game/ui/SceneStage.gd:171, a particle lifetime). `GameState.add_gold()` (game/core/GameState.gd:363) mutates `gold` and emits, keeping no running total, and `reputation_points` (GameState.gd:81) is a spendable-looking balance that docs/03 §6.5's disband penalty can reduce (sim/core/Reputation.gd:308 `rp_after_disband`), so it is not a lifetime figure either. `to_dict()` (GameState.gd:1531-1567) persists neither.

items.area: M5 — quest/achievement board and the endgame after Raid 5
items.remaining_work_note:
DONE. Three counters on GameState that only ever RISE — `gold_earned_lifetime` (every positive `add_gold()`), `rp_earned_lifetime` (incremented at the award in `_award_reputation()`, before docs/03 §6.5's disband penalty can touch the balance) and `items_sold_lifetime` (every `sell_loot()`). Both figures that looked like they could serve instead go DOWN: `gold` is what is left after spending and `reputation_points` is reduced by a disband, so a cap computed from either would shrink as the player played.

ONE READING WAS AVAILABLE AND IS NOW STATED AND TESTED: docs/01 §8.0's opening 60 G is assigned in `new_game()` rather than paid through `add_gold()`, so it is seed capital and NOT income. The other reading is defensible, which is exactly why `test_the_opening_purse_is_seed_capital_and_not_income` exists — otherwise somebody 'fixes' it by routing the purse through add_gold() and the board starts owing a reward to a guild that has done nothing.

SAVE_VERSION 14 -> 15 with all four parts in one commit, because the suite demands every one: the bump, a registered `_v14_to_v15` step (a stamp — the history was never written down by an older build and seeding it from the current balance would be an invented figure dressed as a recovered one), the frozen shape record moved, and a committed v14 fixture at the version left behind. `make_save_fixtures.gd` gained ADDED_IN_V15 and now downgrades v15 -> v14 -> v13 -> v12 -> v11 -> v10; `test_each_fixture_carries_exactly_the_keys_its_version_shipped` gained the v14 row so the older fixtures are still proved to be genuinely older.

Ten tests in test_game_state.gd, including the one that says why this item existed: `Achievements.coin_cap()` has been dividing by `_prop()`'s zero fallback since it was written, so every cap was zero and every claim refusable. 1479 tests, all six stages green.

items.title: Credits content — who the game credits
items.spec_source: docs/10 §13 row 1 names "a victory/report screen and credits"; no doc in the set names a single contributor, and docs/16 §8.2's release checklist does not carry a credits item
items.evidence: `grep -rni "credits" docs/` returns only docs/10-content-and-encounters.md:568 and the docs/16 row that quotes it; there is no contributor list, no third-party licence list and no attribution file anywhere in the repo (no CREDITS, no LICENSE, no THIRD_PARTY in the root listing).

items.title: AC_K and MANA_TO_SPELL are flat consts — the mitigation cap binds from tier 3 and casters run away
items.evidence: sim/core/Formulas.gd:33 `const AC_K := 60.0` and :34 `const MITIGATION_CAP := 0.75`, both flat; :79 `const MANA_TO_SPELL := 0.35`, also flat, used at :176. docs/08:697 states the consequence in the doc's own words: `At index 9, mitigation(541) = 94.7%, clamped to MITIGATION_CAP 0.75. **The cap binds from roughly index 5 onward** (mitigation(107) = 78.1%)`, and recommends `AC_K(tier) = 60 * 1.5^(index)` — marked ❓ OPEN. docs/08:687 raises the paired question: the ×2.00 Mana step per half-tier means `MANA_TO_SPELL must decay 0.85 per tier or Mana's step must come down to ~1.55`, and says `Only one of the two may be written down.` Neither has a docs/15 Q-number: grep for `AC_K` in docs/15 returns only line 95 and line 606, both restating the Tier 1 default of 60. docs/16:371's entry criterion E3.5 lists the item multipliers but says nothing about AC_K.
items.spec_source: docs/08 §10.1, §10.2 (both ❓ OPEN), §11's tuning-lever table
items.risk: Without this, tiers 3/4/5 are mechanically identical in mitigation terms — every tank sits at the 0.75 cap — and the whole late-game boss budget is a straight line. It is also the one change in the slice that can move the golden hashes if the default is not wired as a true no-op.

Both default to tier 1, which is exactly what shipped, so the five golden hashes are unchanged.

TWO MEASUREMENTS CORRECTED THE DOC'S OWN NOTE, and both are in the entry and under test: (a) §9 says the cap binds 'from roughly index 5' off a projected AC of 107 — the real ladder reaches 40 at Tier 3 and only touches the cap at Tier 5 Boss 1; (b) §9 writes the step as 1.5^INDEX over ten rung indices, and read that way it over-shoots to 11.1% tank mitigation by Tier 4 — the ladder's tank AC grows ~x1.55 per TIER, so the step is per tier and holds mitigation at 36-40% across all five.

NOT DONE, deliberately, and tracked as M5-T25-15: threading the tier into the budget derivation and into RaidSim. Those must move in ONE commit or a budget sized with the curve would disagree with fights fought on the flat constant, and neither matters until tiers 2-5 are named and ship (BL-69).

items.title: ContentDB cannot hold more than one tier: the encounter index and raid tables are keyed by slot/class, not by tier
items.evidence:
VERIFIED AGAINST THE TREE 2026-09-11 — THE EVIDENCE BELOW IS STALE. (reconciliation sweep: one agent read this entry and the files it names, and every claim of 'done' was then put to two independent skeptics whose brief was to refute it. Four survived the read and did not survive the refutation.)
Specifically no longer true: "sim/content/ContentDB.gd:361 `_encounters_by_slot[enc.slot] = enc` — the key is the bare slot string (`E1`..`E5`, `A1`..`A3`), so loading a Tier 2 file silently overwrites Tier 1."
What the tree actually shows now:
  - sim/content/ContentDB.gd:527 writes `_encounters_by_slot[slot_key] = enc` where slot_key comes from `static func _slot_key(tier, slot)` at :529-530 returning "%d:%s" % [tier, slot] — the bare-slot key the entry quotes is gone
  - sim/content/ContentDB.gd:540 `func encounter_at(tier: int, slot: String)` exists and :546 `func encounter_at_slot(slot)` is kept as an explicit tier-1 shim returning `encounter_at(1, slot)`, exactly the migration the entry asked for
  - sim/content/ContentDB.gd:478 `raid_tables[tier] = per_class` inside `_load_raid_tables(doc, tier)` (:449) — the grid is tier -> class -> boss; the doc comment at :80-82 names the old failure
  - sim/content/ContentDB.gd:791 `func raid_drops(class_key, encounter, tier: int = 1)` reads `raid_tables.get(tier, {})` and :809 `func best_in_slot_stats(class_key, tier: int = 1)` does the same — both tier-parameterised with the requested default
  - sim/content/ContentDB.gd:27-41 DEFAULT_PATHS now holds only the non-tier files (classes, starting, tutorials, tutorial_items); :116 `static func tier_paths(tier)` builds the four per-tier filenames and :152-163 `static func default_paths()` probes tiers 1..MAX_TIER (:52 MAX_TIER := 5) and fills out["tiers"] — no tier filename is hardcoded anywhere
  - sim/content/ContentDB.gd:206-249 `_load(paths)` iterates `paths.get("tiers", [])` three times (items, raid tables, encounters) instead of the literal `for label in ["starting","adventure","raid"]` the entry quotes; :243 calls `_load_raid_tables(raid_doc, tier)` per manifest entry
  - sim/content/ContentDB.gd:191-193 `_check_tier_header` reports a file whose header tier disagrees with the rung it was mounted at, and :511-514 does the same per encounter record
  - tests/unit/test_content_db.gd:365-369 `_two_tier_db()` mounts `paths["tiers"] = [t1, DB.tier_paths(2)]`; :371-386 test_two_tiers_load_side_by_side asserts adventure_encounters(1)==3, adventure_encounters(2)==3, raid_encounters(1)==5, raid_encounters(2)==5 — the entry's acceptance clause verbatim
  - tests/unit/test_content_db.gd:398-408 test_raid_tables_and_best_in_slot_are_tier_scoped asserts raid_drops("warrior",5,2)[0].id == ITM_T2_RAID_SHIELD_OH, raid_drops(...,3)==[], t1_ac==28 and `t2_ac > t1_ac` — the best_in_slot_stats acceptance clause
  - tests/unit/test_content_db.gd:387-396 test_the_encounter_index_is_keyed_by_tier_and_slot asserts encounter_at(1,"E1").id=="t1_raid_e1" vs encounter_at(2,"E1").id=="t2_raid_e1", encounter_at(3,"E1")==null, and that encounter_at_slot("E1") still means tier 1
  - tests/unit/test_content_db.gd:79-99 test_every_item_every_mounted_file_declares_is_indexed replaced the magic 98 with per-file counts read off the manifest via `_item_files()` (:59-70) and asserts the sum; :101-107 asserts 28 Adventure items per mounted tier by looping DB.default_paths()["tiers"]
  - tests/unit/test_content_db.gd:414-431 test_the_default_manifest_finds_tiers_on_disk_not_in_code checks tier_paths(4) resolves to res://data/encounters_t4.json — docs/16 §7 X2.8 asserted directly
  - THE SEAM IS ARMED, not just defined: game/core/RaidPlan.gd:385-392 `for tier in range(1, int(state.highest_unlocked_tier()) + 1)` calls `state.content.tutorial_encounters(tier)`, `adventure_encounters(tier)`, `raid_encounters(tier)`; game/screens/AdventureBoard.gd:538 returns `RaidPlan.ladder(_state)`; game/ui/Boot.gd:98 calls `ContentDB.load_all()` with no args, which takes the `default_paths()` manifest path
  - sim/core/Loot.gd:198 calls `db.trinket_pool_for(tier)` (defined ContentDB.gd:580), so the per-tier trinket pool built at ContentDB.gd:490 has a live reader
  - data/ holds encounters_t2..t5.json, encounters_adventure_t2..t5.json and items_t2..t5_{adventure,raid}.json; items_t2_raid.json carries 48 items, 9 class_tables and 4 boss5 trinkets, matching the test's `_db.items.size() + 76`. data/tier_words.json marks tiers 2-5 `pending: true`, so `tier_is_named` (ContentDB.gd:137-150) keeps them out of the SHIPPED set by design (docs/15 BL-69) while `tier_paths(n)` still mounts them by name

ORIGINAL EVIDENCE, kept as the record of why this was filed:
sim/content/ContentDB.gd:361 `_encounters_by_slot[enc.slot] = enc` — the key is the bare slot string (`E1`..`E5`, `A1`..`A3`), so loading a Tier 2 file silently overwrites Tier 1. The tier filters at :377-:391 (`if enc != null and enc.tier == tier`) then return an EMPTY array for the losing tier, so `adventure_encounters(1)` would go blank the day tier 2 loads. Same shape at :329 `raid_tables[class_key] = per_boss` — one table per class, not per class per tier; and :489 `best_in_slot_stats(class_key)` iterates it tier-blind. DEFAULT_PATHS (ContentDB.gd:21-27) is a flat six-key dict with the Tier 1 filenames hardcoded, and _load (:108-:140) walks a literal `for label in ["starting", "adventure", "raid"]` then re-reads `paths.get("raid")` singular at :121 for the class tables. The consumer side is already ready and waiting: game/screens/AdventureBoard.gd:413 loops `for tier in range(1, _state.highest_unlocked_tier() + 1)` with the comment `the day Tier 2 content lands it appears here on its own`, and sim/core/Loot.gd:92/:107/:154 already filter every pool by `it.tier == encounter.tier`. tests/unit/test_content_db.gd:35 asserts `_db.items.size(), 98` and will fail on the first new item file.

TWO REAL DEFECTS CAME OUT OF RUNNING IT, both now ruled and tested:
- BL-70: the first generated rung INVERTED at the slot level. warrior_bard legs went 5 AC / 6 HP to 5 / 6 (flat) and monk_rogue legs went 5 / 6 to 5 / 5 (a downgrade) between the Tier 1 raid rung and the Tier 2 Adventure rung, because §13.2 steps the family TOTAL and §13.4 re-splits it, so a share plus rounding can leave one slot behind. TierScaling.floor_against_previous() floors every generated slot against the rung below and nudges a flat slot by one point; it only ever adds, and canon rungs never pass through it.
- BL-69: ContentDB.default_paths() discovers tiers by filename, so generating them SHIPPED 336 items called 'TIER2's Boots' into the live content set in one command (three existing tests caught it). A tier now mounts only when data/tier_words.json says its words are answered; the files are still written, still tested, still loadable by name.

One discrepancy recorded rather than fixed: docs/09 §12.1 writes the id format with ONE optional variant segment and canon's own Tier 1 file ships two (ITM_T1_RAID_W1H_MH_SWORD_BASIC). The data is canon and the doc is the summary, so the test accepts one or more.

TWO OF THE AUDIT'S OWN RULES WERE WRONG AND ARE RECORDED AS SUCH:
- COVERAGE cannot demand all four role groups. The only mechanic that stresses SUPPORT is M10 Mana Burn, and docs/10 §473 gives Tier 1 M01-M06/M08/M09 — so the obvious reading fails canon's own tier, which is why the shipped test only ever listed three. Enforced as: the three groups Tier 1's vocabulary can stress must be stressed before the boss, AND the boss must not be the first fight to test any group. The second half is where the design intent lives.
- THE LADDER is compared SLOT BY SLOT, not 'tier N+1's E1 beats tier N's E5'. E1 is a twelve-round pull and E5 a twenty-two-round boss, so Tier 2's E1 (4300 HP) legitimately holds less than Tier 1's E5 (7150). The obvious rule would reject canon's own ladder; a test documents the comparison that is NOT made.

items.title: Q-43 — Warrior/Bard Mana variants are 'Tier 2+ intent' and must be a generator rule, not an afterthought
items.evidence: docs/15:471 records the decision: canon's own note says `Mana can appear on these pieces and compete with Power` but no Tier 1 piece has any, and the recommended default is `**Treat as Tier 2+ intent**`. Confirmed in data: `data/items_t1_adventure.json` and `data/items_t1_raid.json` contain zero warrior_bard_* rows with a `mana` stat. docs/09 §13.4 (line 765) gives Power for physical families and Mana for none of them, so the generator as specified would carry the Tier 1 zero forward through all four remaining tiers and quietly kill the decision. The dependency is real: docs/15:479 Q-46 notes the Bard has `neither a mechanic nor a primary stat` until songs land.
items.remaining_work: Add a `mana_variants` block to `data/tier_scaling.json` so the rule lives with the other multipliers: from rung r3 (Tier 2 Adventure) onward, emit ONE additional warrior_bard item per slot carrying Mana in place of some AC, at the same total budget — id suffix `_MANA` per docs/09 §12.1's VARIANT field, which already lists `MANA` as a legal value. Magnitude: give the variant the family's Mana total at that rung computed by the healer line's Mana step, and reduce its AC by the §13.4 share it displaces, so the two variants are a genuine choice rather than a strict upgrade. This adds 4 rows per Adventure rung and 4 per Raid rung from r3 up = 32 items, which must be folded into M5-T25-06's monotonicity assertions as a SIBLING comparison (variant vs variant across tiers) rather than a same-slot one, or assertion (1) will fire on every variant pair. Gate it behind a `mana_variants: true` switch in tier_scaling.json so the `Never` reading from docs/15 Q-43 stays selectable, per the project's ambiguity-behind-a-switch rule.

items.title: docs/07 does not spec the nine Legendary quirks at all — this is a missing SPEC, not missing code
items.evidence: `grep -ci quirk docs/07-combat-simulation.md` → 0. The word does not appear once in the owning doc. docs/04-recruitment-and-roster.md:493 is the only contract: "| `quirk` | record | One class-flavoured mechanical gift; specced in doc 07, named here |". docs/15-open-questions.md:1384-1402 records this exactly (Q-58 OPEN - needs docs/07), and every one of the nine data files carries a self-describing `quirk.status` of "❓ OPEN — … docs/07 does not spec it yet. Inert until it does" (e.g. data/legendaries/shaman.json quirk block). So the BACKLOG.md:107 line "docs/07's nine Legendary quirk specs, then turn them on" is accurate and the work is NOT implementation. The nine as authored (id | name | reads_as): quirk_warrior | Holds the Line | never yields the main-tank slot; quirk_cleric | One More Cast | finds mana that was not, strictly, there; quirk_shaman | The Totem Holds | her buffs outlast the pull that placed them; quirk_druid | Grows Into the Gap | covers whichever role the party is short of; quirk_mage | Second Wind of Fire | first spell after a wipe recovery lands harder; quirk_wizard | Reads the Whole Fight | knows the enrage timer without being told; quirk_rogue | Never Where the Boss Looks | draws less attention than the numbers say; quirk_monk | Reads the Room | notices a mechanic one beat before anyone else; quirk_bard | Carries the Beat | keeps the melee swinging in time through a phase change.
items.remaining_work: A HUMAN must author the spec; a build loop writing it would be inventing nine permanent combat effects on the strictly-best rarity, which is the exact thing docs/15 Q-58 refused ("That is a design pass, not content work"). What the person must produce, per quirk: (1) trigger condition in the sim's own vocabulary (round/phase from docs/07 §4.1, roll site from §5.3, mechanic id from Enums.Mechanic, mistake type id from sim/core/Mistakes.gd TYPES); (2) magnitude as a number or basis-point delta, with the doc-08-style coefficient named; (3) whether it is always-on or once-per-encounter; (4) an explicit statement of what it must NOT do (a quirk that changes the wipe rate of the docs/10 §5.3 benchmark twelve by more than a stated band is out of budget). Write it as a new docs/07 §12 "Legendary quirks" (or docs/06 §4.10 — see Q58-2, ownership is genuinely ambiguous) with 🔷 PROPOSED markers, cite it from docs/04 §11.2's table row, then flip docs/15 Q-58 from OPEN to DECIDED. Only after that: delete the `quirk.status` line from all nine data files and implement against the seam in Q58-4. ACCEPTANCE: the balance sweep (tools/balance_sweep.gd, the 1,440-run grid) reruns and the clear-rate of the benchmark twelve moves inside the band the new doc section states; tests/golden/e5_legendaries_raid.json is regenerated by tools/write_goldens.gd and the diff is reviewed line by line rather than accepted wholesale, because that scenario is the one that contains Legendaries.
items.risk: A quirk is a permanent buff on the rarity that is already the best in the game, and the mistake-chance scale it would sit on is itself declared unanchored: docs/07 §5.3 says "Until doc 08 §12 is amended, treat every mistake percentage in the project as unanchored and do not tune against it." Any quirk expressed as a mistake-chance delta (monk, and arguably warrior) is being tuned against a number the project has disowned.

items.title: Five of the nine quirks name mechanics the sim does not have — the substrate audit the spec pass needs first
items.evidence: Read against sim/core/RaidSim.gd (823 lines) and sim/core/Formulas.gd. HAS SUBSTRATE (4): quirk_warrior — `_assign_tanks()` at RaidSim.gd:228 sets `is_main_tank`, and MIS_AGGRO / MIS_TAUNT_LAPSE exist at Mistakes.gd:50,57, so "never yields the main-tank slot" is expressible as immunity to the aggro-loss mistake types or as a floor under `c.threat`. quirk_rogue — threat is real: `c.add_threat(int(round(Formulas.threat_from(...))))` at RaidSim.gd:450 and `_pick_enemy_target()` at RaidSim.gd:362 picks top threat, so "draws less attention" is a multiplier on `Formulas.threat_from`. quirk_monk — `Mistakes.roll(...)` at RaidSim.gd:437 already takes a `relief_bp` argument (RaidSim.gd:705 `_relief_bp`) that docs/11 §7's Steady Hands feeds, so "notices a mechanic one beat early" is an existing parameter. quirk_shaman's CLASS has a hook (`Formulas.shaman_chain_heal` via `_cast_heal` RaidSim.gd:497) but its stated effect does not — see below. NO SUBSTRATE (5): quirk_shaman "buffs outlast the pull" — there is no buff or duration system anywhere; `grep -n 'buff\|aura\|totem' sim/core/Formulas.gd sim/core/RaidSim.gd sim/model/Combatant.gd` returns nothing, and the chain heal is instantaneous. quirk_bard "keeps the melee swinging through a phase change" — the Bard has no song, no buff and no ability at all (its only appearances in the sim are the melee coefficient Formulas.gd:130 and the action-order rank at RaidSim.gd:419), AND there is no "phase change" concept — the closest is `Enums.Mechanic.ENRAGE` at RaidSim.gd:311. It is doubly blocked: docs/06 §5 "The Bard problem ❓ OPEN" has not chosen between B1/B2/B3, and docs/07 OQ-10 says "Bard … is flagged as not-shippable until the class doc lands." quirk_cleric "finds mana that was not, strictly, there" — mana is a magnitude stat fed into `Formulas.cleric_heal(heal_base, mana)`, never a pool that depletes; docs/07 §11 OQ-1 is still unresolved on this exact point ("Mana is both: a pool that depletes and a magnitude stat … Revisit with doc 08"), so the quirk presupposes an unbuilt, undecided resource. quirk_mage "first spell after a wipe recovery lands harder" — there is no in-encounter recovery event; downed/dead exist (`Combatant.is_downed()`) but nothing marks "the raid recovered", and a WIPE ends the encounter (`_check_end` RaidSim.gd:790). quirk_wizard "knows the enrage timer without being told" — ENRAGE fires at RaidSim.gd:311-318, but the sim has no pre-enrage decision to inform: no cooldowns to hold, no burn phase, no retreat. quirk_druid "covers whichever role the party is short of" — role is fixed by class (`role_group` baked into the gear profile at RaidSim.gd:180) and the only role fallback is the tank backstop at RaidSim.gd:246-256.
items.remaining_work: Hand the designer this table with the spec pass (Q58-1) and force a choice per quirk in the NO-SUBSTRATE five: either (a) restate the effect against a mechanic that exists — e.g. shaman becomes "the chain heal's third bounce never fizzles" (MIS_CHAIN_FIZZLE at Mistakes.gd:88 is real, and docs/04:397's own worked example already writes exactly that: `quirk: chain_heal_never_misses_third_target`), cleric becomes "immune to MIS_HEAL_CORPSE", mage becomes "+X% spell damage while any ally is downed", wizard becomes "+X% damage from the round the enrage lands", druid becomes "counts as a valid main-tank fallback in `_assign_tanks`"; or (b) build the subsystem, which is a doc-06/doc-07 change and an order of magnitude more work. NOTE for the designer: docs/04:397's Natsuna example ALREADY contains a fully-formed quirk in shape (a) that the data file's `quirk_shaman` silently disagrees with — that contradiction should be resolved in the same pass. quirk_bard must be deferred outright and recorded as such: docs/06 §5 and docs/07 OQ-10 both block it, so eight quirks can ship and the ninth cannot. ACCEPTANCE: every quirk in the finished spec names a function that exists in sim/ today, or names the doc section that will create it.
