VERIFIED AGAINST THE TREE 2026-09-11 — WHAT IS ACTUALLY LEFT:
Three of the five sub-items and the acceptance test are outstanding.

(a) The seam is UNARMED — the classic false positive. All four hooks exist in sim/core/Quirks.gd and are identity-valued, but no production file calls any of them. Specifically still to wire: `Quirks.threat_multiplier()` around the `Formulas.threat_from` result before `c.add_threat()` in RaidSim's round loop; `Quirks.relief_bp_bonus()` folded into `_relief_bp()` (RaidSim.gd:1855); `Quirks.tank_priority()` in `_assign_tanks()` (RaidSim.gd:342); `Quirks.immune_to()` in `Mistakes.eligible_types()` (Mistakes.gd:235).

(b) Item (5) is untouched: `RaidSim.run()` (RaidSim.gd:195) still takes `(roster, encounter, db, seed_value, ...)` and ContentDB has no LegendaryPool member at all, so nothing inside sim/core can turn `Raider.legendary_def_id` into a quirk id. The pool-through-db threading has not started.

(c) The ACCEPTANCE condition is entirely unmet: there is no tests/unit/test_quirks.gd and no test anywhere names Quirks or any hook. Needed: a test asserting all four hooks return their identity value for all nine quirk ids at BOTH flag settings; a direct test that the nine ids are distinct and equal `quirk_<class_key>`; and the golden SHA-256 assertion in test_golden.gd tied to the seam (test_golden.gd:78 already hashes `full_log_sha256`, but nothing connects it to the quirks flag).

Note for the planner: build/plan/handoff-quirks.md:131 explicitly instructs NOT to wire (a)/(b) until `Quirks.SPECS` has rows and docs/15 BL-58 is decided. If that deferral stands, this item should be re-scoped to (c) only — the test file — because (c) is cheap, blocked by nothing, and is the thing that would stop the two false docstrings (Quirks.gd:21-22 and handoff-quirks.md:134) from claiming coverage that does not exist.

THE ORIGINAL PLAN, kept for the HOW — some of its clauses are already met, see above for which:
Land the seam now, with every effect a no-op, so Q58-1's output is a table plus one function rather than a refactor. (1) `LegendaryPool.quirk_of(class_id) -> Dictionary` returning the record, alongside the existing `morale_rules(class_id)`. (2) Extend `LegendaryPool._validate()`: quirk must be a Dictionary with non-empty `id`, `name`, `reads_as`; `id` must be unique across the nine (same failure shape as the existing duplicate-class check at :47); and while Q-58 is OPEN, `status` must be present — a test that fails the moment somebody removes `status` without docs/07 having a §12 is the honest guard, mirroring the existing name-invention guard. (3) Do NOT add a field to Raider: `Raider.legendary_def_id` plus the pool is enough to resolve the quirk, so no save-shape change and no SAVE_VERSION bump. (4) New `sim/core/Quirks.gd`: `const ENABLED := false`, a `SPECS := {}` registry keyed by quirk id, and four pure hook functions called from the sites the audit found — `threat_multiplier(raider) -> float` at RaidSim.gd:450, `relief_bp_bonus(raider) -> float` folded into `_relief_bp()` at RaidSim.gd:705, `tank_priority(raider) -> int` in `_assign_tanks()` at RaidSim.gd:228, and `immune_to(raider, type_id) -> bool` consulted in `Mistakes.eligible_types()`. All four return the identity value while ENABLED is false. (5) `RaidSim.run()` needs the pool: pass it through `db` (ContentDB) rather than loading it inside sim/core, so the sim stays a pure function of its arguments (docs/14 §3.1). ACCEPTANCE: copy the pattern tests/unit/test_consumables.gd already uses for the empty loadout — assert the five golden files in tests/golden/ are byte-identical (SHA-256) with the seam in and ENABLED false, so the quirks cannot move a number until somebody turns them on; plus a test that all nine quirk ids are distinct and match `quirk_<class_key>`.

items.evidence: The predicate exists — game/core/GameState.gd:967-972 `_refresh_big_dumb()` sets `r.big_dumb_active = int(r.consecutive_benched) >= BENCHED_RUNS_IS_BIG_DUMB` (5). The counter does not. `grep -rn consecutive_benched --include=*.gd .` returns exactly five hits and NONE is a write: sim/model/Raider.gd:122 (declaration), :325 (to_dict), :382 (from_dict), game/core/GameState.gd:959 (comment), :972 (the read). It is initialised to 0, saved as 0, loaded as 0, forever. docs/15-open-questions.md:1417 therefore states something false: "| 1 | Benched for 5 consecutive runs | **Live** — `Raider.consecutive_benched` already counts it exactly |", and BUILD_STATE.md:246 and BACKLOG.md:106 repeat it. THREE more counters have the same defect: sim/core/RaidSim.gd:815-822 `_queue_deltas()` builds `{raider_id, runs_attended, wipes_witnessed, died}` into `result.deltas_queued`, and `grep -rn deltas_queued --include=*.gd .` shows it is read ONLY by tests/unit/test_raid_sim.gd:130,132 — game/core/GameState.record_attempt() never applies it, so `runs_attended` and `wipes_witnessed` are permanently 0 while game/screens/RaiderDetail.gd:630-632 renders them to the player. `loot_received` is likewise never incremented (assign_loot at GameState.gd:~1010 equips and returns). And the `benched` morale trigger, fully specced at sim/core/Morale.gd:201-204 (-2, TOTAL_WINDOW, limit 6, window 7, "from the 2nd consecutive tick") with its backstory amplifier at sim/content/BackstoryPool.gd:246, is never fired: GameState._apply_raid_morale() (GameState.gd:557-575) fires only `brought`, `cleared`, `wipe` and `knocked_out`, all on `last_party`, and touches nobody on the bench.
items.risk: Firing `benched` puts a new recurring negative on every bench-warmer, which is a live morale-balance change: docs/15 Q-34 measured a wipe spiral at -10.8 per wipe against +1.125 drift per tick, and -2 per run on the bench pushes the same direction. The golden files are sim-only so they should not move, but tests/unit/test_morale_leaving.gd and tests/unit/test_full_loop.gd will need re-checking, and `rest_until_recovered()` (GameState.gd:630) may take more ticks to settle a large roster. Land the counters first, the `benched` trigger second, so a regression is attributable.

(a) three wipes on three different rungs -> peak 3, `big_dumb_active`, reasons has `bullet_3_this_tier` and not `wiped_3`, warning line carries row 4's wording; (b) two wipes at Tier 1, `reputation_rank = KNOWN` (Tier 2), third wipe -> `bullet_tier` 2, peak 1, not big dumb (exercises GameState.gd:1895-1897); (c) four benched runs fire "benched" three times — the control Common with `hates_being_benched` is credited, Natsuna is not, no row opened. items.title: BIG-dumb condition #5 — upkeep and payday do not exist in code OR in the doc that owns them; Q-31 says 'per-run' while §11.3 says 'payday'
items.evidence: `grep -rn 'upkeep\|payday' --include=*.gd game sim` returns one hit and it is a comment (game/core/GameState.gd:961). Worse, the owning doc never wrote the spec: `grep -n upkeep docs/11-economy-and-crafting.md` returns NOTHING, and docs/11 §4.2's sink table (lines 106-124) runs S1..S14 — recruiting, tavern refresh, buy a round, consumables, two comfort lines, three building tracks, equipment upgrades, crafting ×2, wipe fee, buy-back — with no wages row. docs/15-open-questions.md:454 rules Q-31 DECIDED as "**Small per-run upkeep scaling with rarity, charged on benched raiders too.** Magnitudes owned by doc 11" — an owner that never delivered. And the two decisions contradict each other on cadence: Q-31 and docs/04 Q8 (line 649) say PER RUN, while docs/04 §11.3 condition 5 (line 516) and docs/04 §12.2's Payday row (line 560, itself hedged "if doc 11 adopts upkeep") say PAYDAY — "gold at 0 on payday for 2 consecutive paydays" is meaningless without a fixed cadence, which a per-run charge does not have. Numbering defect on top: docs/15:1421's link `[Q-31](#q-31)` resolves to the section headed "### Q-31 - Duplicate protection, with no mechanism given" at docs/15:1066, not to the upkeep row at :454 — there are two Q-31s.
items.remaining_work: A PERSON must settle three things before any code is written; a loop inventing them would be setting the game's only recurring gold sink by guess, and that sink is what decides whether the roster cap and the bench mean anything (docs/04 §12.1's stated reason for a cap of 15). (1) Rule the cadence: per-run charge, or a payday every N Day Ticks — and if payday, give N. This is the fork that makes condition #5 expressible at all. (2) Write docs/11 §4.2 an S15 row: per-rarity Tier-1 magnitudes, whether benched raiders pay (Q-31 says yes), and re-run §4.3's income-vs-cost curve and §4.4's "gold-constrained, 0-20% carried balance at each tier boundary" target, because a recurring sink across 15-20 raiders is large next to the ~100 G-per-Raid-1 anchor. (3) Fix the duplicate Q-31 numbering in docs/15 so the cross-reference resolves. ONLY THEN the code, which is small: `Economy.upkeep_for(raider, tier) -> int` in sim/core/Economy.gd; a `_resolve_payday()` called from `_resolve_day_tick()` (game/core/GameState.gd:869) on the ruled cadence; `var payday_misses: int = 0` on GameState, incremented when a payday resolves with the bill unpayable, reset to 0 on any paid payday, saved with a SAVE_VERSION bump; predicate `payday_misses >= 2` in `_refresh_big_dumb()`. ACCEPTANCE: two consecutive unpayable paydays set `big_dumb_active` on a Legendary and one paid payday in between does not.
items.risk: This is the largest balance change in the slice and it is not really a Legendary feature — upkeep touches every screen with a price on it and the whole §4.3 curve. Condition #5 is a two-line consequence of a subsystem nobody has scoped; do not let the Legendary item pull the economy pass in behind it. If the designer is unavailable, the correct build-loop action is to LEAVE condition #5 false and say so in docs/15, exactly as Q-59 already does.

items.title: docs/04 §11.4's warning surface is unbuilt — `big_dumb_active` is computed and saved but never shown to the player
items.evidence: docs/04-recruitment-and-roster.md:519 (§11.4) requires "a hard, unmissable confirmation the *first* time a Legendary crosses below 40, and a persistent roster warning while any BIG-dumb condition is active. Losing a hand-authored character should be a story the player tells, but it must never be a surprise." Nothing implements either: `grep -rn 'BIG dumb\|big_dumb' game/screens/` returns nothing, and the only Legendary-aware UI in the whole game/screens tree is game/screens/Tavern.gd:271-272's "1 of 1" stamp. `Raider.big_dumb_active` (sim/model/Raider.gd:74) is written by GameState.gd:972, read by sim/core/Morale.gd:319 and :333, saved at Raider.gd:316/352 — and never rendered. There is also no "which condition" information anywhere: `_refresh_big_dumb()` collapses everything to one bool, so even a screen that wanted to name the reason could not.
items.remaining_work: Change `_refresh_big_dumb()` to record WHY as well as whether — a `var big_dumb_reasons: Dictionary` on GameState, `raider_id -> Array[String]` of condition ids ("benched_5", "wiped_3", "wishlist_insult_2", "bullet_3_this_tier", "unpaid_2_paydays"), derived each refresh and therefore NOT saved (it is a pure function of the counters, like `comfort_floor`). Then two surfaces, both inside the test contract (screen tests collect only Label.text and Button.text and press buttons by text fragment): (1) a persistent Label on game/screens/RaiderDetail.gd and on the roster row naming the active condition in words — "AT RISK: benched 5 runs running" — visible while any reason is present; (2) a one-shot confirmation the first time a Legendary's morale crosses below 40, built as a Label plus a Button whose text a test can press, with a saved `var legendary_warned: Array = []` of raider ids so "the first time" means once ever (SAVE_VERSION bump, shared with the other counter work). ACCEPTANCE: a screen test that sets a Legendary's `big_dumb_active` and asserts the roster and detail screens both contain a Label naming the condition; a test that the confirmation appears once and not on the second crossing. NOTE the sequencing: until Q59-0 lands, no condition can ever become true, so this screen would be dead code — build it after Q59-0.
items.risk: Verify the Roster screen's real filename before editing (the screens directory was not enumerated in this audit beyond the files grepped); the warning must land on whichever screen owns the roster rows. Keep every string in a Label or a Button or the screen tests cannot see it.

  - Corroborating tests: tests/unit/test_event_log.gd:47/69/86/105/128/147/160/176/193/225/238/259/274/296 all call emit_mistake with MIS_* keys; :130 `assert_eq(e.mistake["type"], "MIS_TAUNT_LAPSE")`, :164 `assert_eq(e.mistake["template"], "MIS_AGGRO.01")`, :206 `assert_true(d.has("template_id"), "the line to render is referenced, not inlined")`. tests/unit/test_mistake_lines.gd:87 asserts `mistake["template"]` is non-empty on real sim output and :141-142 resolves the variant back through the corpus.
  - The audit's own grep-scope claim is stale too: `emit_mistake` now appears at sim/core/EventLog.gd:192, sim/core/RaidSim.gd:1723, tests/unit/test_event_log.gd (14 sites) and tests/unit/test_log_player.gd:55,:57,:374 — not the three sites the entry lists.

ORIGINAL EVIDENCE, kept as the record of why this was filed:
sim/core/RaidSim.gd:606-608 `_log_mistake` calls `log.emit_mistake(round_no, phase, c, ev.type_name, ev.severity_name(), ...)` — it passes `ev.type_name` ("Pulled Aggro Off the Tank"), not `ev.type_id` ("MIS_AGGRO"). sim/core/EventLog.gd:151-159 stores that string as `mistake["type"]`. Confirmed in the goldens: tests/golden/e1_commons_starting.json story reads `[R01] Kel MISTAKE · Moderate · Pulled Aggro Off the Tank`. Separately, docs/07 §5.1's MistakeEvent struct lists `log_template_id`, and sim/core/Mistakes.gd:157-170 (class MistakeEvent) has no such field. RaidSim.gd:607 is the ONLY `emit_mistake` call site in the codebase (grep `emit_mistake` → sim/core/EventLog.gd:151, sim/core/RaidSim.gd:607, tests/unit/test_log_player.gd:45-46).
items.risk: Golden churn. Do this alone, in one commit, with `story` arrays byte-identical and only `full_log_sha256` moving — otherwise the diff that proves the comedy pass is correct is buried under a diff that proves nothing.

THE PLAN THIS ENTRY WAS CARRYING, kept because it is the record of what was asked for:
Make the event carry what a renderer needs, before any writing happens. (1) Add `var log_template_id: String = ""` to `Mistakes.MistakeEvent` (sim/core/Mistakes.gd:157) and include it in `MistakeEvent.to_dict()` (line ~178) — docs/07 §5.1 already names the field. items.title: The writing pass: 192 lines across 18 types, with a measured per-type budget, not the doc's flat 6
items.evidence: Doc floor: docs/07:530 rule 4 "Each mistake type needs at least 6 template variants so a long raid does not repeat"; docs/14:487 `log_templates | array[string] | ≥6 required`; docs/14:536 assertion 7. MEASURED reality contradicts the floor — counting mistake lines per type inside a single encounter in tests/golden/: e5_miserable_commons (16 rounds, 64 mistakes) fires `Went AFK` 13×, `Attacked the Wrong Target` 11×, `Healed the Wrong Target` 10×, `Forgot to Taunt` 9×, `Pulled Aggro` 9×, `Argument` 7×; e1_commons_starting (22 rounds, 52 mistakes) fires `Forgot to Taunt` 12×, `Pulled Aggro` 9×, `Healed the Wrong Target` 8×. docs/15 Q-21 (RESOLVED) records the post-rescale worst sweep cell at 144 mistakes/encounter, ~2.25× e5_miserable_commons — so a hot type can plausibly reach ~29 in one fight. Six variants would repeat verbatim twice in a raid the player watches tonight.
items.risk: docs/16 R-3 names this the project's top risk and calls it "a content and writing risk, not a code risk" — the taxonomy can be perfect and the game still not funny. A build loop can DRAFT all 192; it cannot certify them funny. Pair with M5-COMEDY-12.

The nine legendary definition files already carry a hand-authored voice channel — `data/legendaries/shaman.json` has `dialogue_barks: ["Data. Set it down and we go again.", "You were terrible. I was worse. Come here.", "The totem stays. So do we."]` — but no `mistake_lines` key on any of the nine (keys are: schema_version, _source, _notes, legendary_def_id, class_id, display_name, name_pending, name_status, portrait_set, starting_morale, recruit_cost_override, gear_grant, quirk, backstory, morale_rules, dialogue_barks). tests/golden/e5_legendaries_raid.json: 2 mistakes across 17 rounds, so the volume needed per legendary is tiny.
items.risk: None mechanical. The naming rule is the trap: a funny legendary line is much easier to write with a name in it, and eight of them may not have one.

items.title: The joke line is never rendered anywhere: RaidView's branch is dead, describe() and Results omit it entirely
items.evidence:
VERIFIED AGAINST THE TREE 2026-09-11 — THE EVIDENCE BELOW IS STALE. (reconciliation sweep: one agent read this entry and the files it names, and every claim of 'done' was then put to two independent skeptics whose brief was to refute it. Four survived the read and did not survive the refutation.)
Specifically no longer true: "game/screens/RaidView.gd:900-909 renders the joke only `if not joke_text.is_empty()`, where `joke_text := String(e.params.get("text", ""))`. Nothing ever puts "text" in a mistake entry's params ... Confirmed by the goldens, whose `story` arrays are pure headers."
What the tree actually shows now:

The constant's comment says what it is FOR: a placeholder detector, sitting far below the shortest shipped line (103 characters), whose only job is to refuse 'TBD' — never to judge whether a joke lands, which is docs/16 R-3's human gate.

(b) THE TWO MISSING CHECKS EXIST. Every encounter in `data/` carries a usable line, and no two share one — the copy-paste failure the field exists to prevent, which passes every other check in the project. Both walk the FILES rather than a loaded ContentDB, deliberately: docs/15 BL-69 keeps an unnamed tier out of the default mount, so a DB-based check would have seen ten of forty-two and called it complete.

(c) THE ONE-SENTENCE CONTRADICTION IS SETTLED AND RECORDED, as docs/15 BL-76. docs/10 §6 said 'One sentence'; five of the ten hand-authored Tier 1 lines are two or three, and they are the better writing — setup then punchline, where the one-sentence ones reach the same shape with a dash. The doc moved to 'one or two sentences' and the row points at the ruling. Sentence count is deliberately NOT tested: a test counting full stops would be policing prose, and §6's stated purpose is the cut rule ('if it cannot be filled in, the encounter is a chore and should be cut'), which is about whether a fight has a joke at all.

items.title: Procedural SFX generator for docs/13 §12.4's eleven UI hooks — no sample exists and none can be sourced
items.evidence:
VERIFIED AGAINST THE TREE 2026-09-11 — THE EVIDENCE BELOW IS STALE. (reconciliation sweep: one agent read this entry and the files it names, and every claim of 'done' was then put to two independent skeptics whose brief was to refute it. Four survived the read and did not survive the refutation.)
Specifically no longer true: "No `.wav`/`.ogg` anywhere in the repo (`find` above)."
What the tree actually shows now:
  - tools/audio/gen_sfx.py exists (446 lines): SR=44100, PARAMS dict with one entry per sampled hook, HOOKS list of docs/13 §12.4's eleven names, DUCK_ONLY={"ui.silence"}, _render()/_finish()/_write_wav() (mono, sampwidth 2, framerate SR), filename(), manifest(), and a main() with --out/--list. Seeds from sha256("<hook>:<index>") so renders are byte-identical.
  - game/assets/audio/sfx/ holds 17 .wav files plus 17 matching .import records: ui_tab, ui_row_select_1/2, ui_chalk_1/2/3, ui_chalk_bad, ui_stamp_1/2/3, ui_seal, ui_coin_1/2, ui_page_turn, ui_ledger_close, ui_blot_1/2 — ten of the eleven hooks, exactly as the acceptance sentence requires.
  - game/core/Audio.gd:75 HOOKS binds all eleven names; Audio.gd:93-97 gives ui.stamp three streams and pitch_jitter_semitones 2.0; Audio.gd:121-124 makes ui.silence a stream-less entry with duck_db -60.0 / duck_seconds 0.4, and Audio.gd:386-388 routes play("ui.silence") into duck() (defined Audio.gd:328) rather than a sample.
  - tools/audio/README.md (122 lines) records the physical model and every parameter per hook in a table, the material rule from §12.4, the 44.1 kHz / mono / 16-bit / fade spec, the house choice that non-indulgent one-shots stay inside 140 ms, and the re-render + `--import` procedure.
  - tests/unit/test_audio.gd asserts the acceptance conditions and more: test_every_hook_with_a_sample_names_a_file_that_is_really_there uses ResourceLoader.exists(); test_the_stamp_is_the_signature_sound_the_doc_specifies asserts 3 variants, 2.0 semitones and <=0.140 s; test_no_generated_sample_is_an_orphan walks res://game/assets/audio/sfx; test_no_sample_is_stereo_or_off_rate asserts mix_rate 44100 and stereo false; test_the_generator_is_in_the_tree_and_documents_itself asserts tools/audio/gen_sfx.py and tools/audio/README.md exist and that the generator names all eleven hooks. tests/run_tests.gd:70-85 discovers tests/ recursively by the test_*.gd name rule, so this file really runs.
  - THE GAP: tools/build_art.sh parses only --clean (line 15) and --gen (line 16); `grep -i audio tools/build_art.sh` returns nothing, and a repo-wide grep for `gen_sfx` hits only build/plan/*.md, build/plan/audit.json, tests/unit/test_audio.gd and tools/audio/ itself. No build script — build_art.sh, verify.sh or export_build.sh — invokes the generator. This is the classic unarmed seam: the instrument is complete and nothing calls it.
  - The entry's evidence sentence "No `.wav`/`.ogg` anywhere in the repo" is false — 17 .wav files are committed under game/assets/audio/sfx/ — and actual_status "not-started" is wrong.

ORIGINAL EVIDENCE, kept as the record of why this was filed:
No `.wav`/`.ogg` anywhere in the repo (`find` above). The project already generates every other asset from script: tools/art/*.py (numpy + PIL — see tools/art/refdiff.py:27 `import numpy as np`) and tools/aseprite/*.lua, driven by tools/build_art.sh. docs/13 §12.4 constrains the palette hard: "All UI sound is *material*: paper, chalk, brass, wax, coin. **No synthesized blips**", and `ui.stamp` must be "≤ 140ms, three round-robin variants, ±2 semitone random pitch". BACKLOG.md:167 already anticipates this: "Generate procedurally or source CC0".
items.risk: Two real risks. (1) 'material, not blips' is a taste judgement a build loop cannot self-verify; mitigate by writing the physical model down in the README and keeping the parameters in one dict so a human can re-tune without re-deriving. (2) `ui.stamp` fires dozens of times per raid — the fatigue requirement (§12.4) is the hard part, and it is the one an autonomous loop is most likely to get wrong. Ship it, then flag it for human review (see AUD-05).

items.title: Music beds, the per-rank town soundscape and the Legendary leitmotif — assign an owner, then compose
items.evidence: docs/15-open-questions.md:593, in §8 "Ownership gaps — nobody owns these at all": "**Audio and music** | The word 'music' appears nowhere in the doc set ... defers mixing to 'audio's call' — to nobody", with the recommendation "**Assign an owner.**" The commitments already made are concrete: docs/02-town-and-buildings.md:349-354 gives every reputation rank an Audio column (Unknown "Wind, one dog, sparse lute" → Known "Lute gains a drum" → Respected "Anvil ring loop, market chatter" → Renowned "Bell toll on entry" → Legendary "Cheer stinger on entry; leitmotif"). None of it exists.
items.remaining_work: SPLIT. The generable half is not blocked and should be done under AUD-03's tool: ambience loops are filtered-noise and granular material (wind, rain on puddles, crowd murmur, an anvil ring, a dog) and `tools/audio/gen_amb.py` can produce seamless 30-60s loops the same way gen_sfx.py produces one-shots, keyed by rank so `Town.gd` picks its bed from `_state.reputation_rank`. The genuinely blocked half is MELODIC: 'sparse lute', 'lute gains a drum', the Renowned bell toll, the Legendary cheer stinger and — above all — the leitmotif. A leitmotif is an authored theme that must be recognisable and must carry the game's tone; procedural generation produces something that is technically music and audibly not a theme, and shipping that is worse than shipping silence. WHAT A PERSON MUST DO: (1) name an audio owner (docs/15 §8's own recommendation); (2) decide whether the five rank beds are composed, licensed CC0, or cut for 1.0; (3) if composed, deliver five stems at 44.1 kHz that loop seamlessly, plus the leitmotif in a form the Legendary stinger can quote. Until then: implement the ambience loops, leave `Audio.play_bed()` a no-op for the melodic beds, and record the decision as a new numbered Q in docs/15 (see AUD-06) rather than inventing a musical direction — canon is silent and BUILD_STATE invariant 3 forbids inventing.
items.risk: The ambience half can ship autonomously and should not be held hostage to the composed half. Do not let a build loop 'solve' the leitmotif with a generated arpeggio.

items.title: docs/13 §12.2's motion table vs M5 'the desk does not move' is an unresolved contradiction — no transition can be built until it is ruled
items.evidence: Two canon-adjacent statements disagree. docs/13 §12.2 (docs/13-ui-ux.md:628) requires "Screen / tab change | Cross-dissolve + active tab shifts 6px right | 110ms | ease-out". docs/13 §2 M5 (docs/13-ui-ux.md:69) says "**The desk does not move.** No screen slides in from off-camera", and the 2026-09-09 supersession note at docs/13-ui-ux.md:45 explicitly preserves it: "M5 ('the desk does not move') survives: the router still has no transitions." game/core/ScreenRouter.gd:4-7 hard-codes that reading in its own docstring: "That is why this router has no transition animation and **never will**". A cross-dissolve is not a slide, so §12.2 and M5 are arguably compatible — but the router's docstring closes the door on both, and nothing records which reading governs.
items.remaining_work: Do NOT silently add a dissolve — the router's docstring says 'never will', and overriding it by fiat is exactly the failure mode the project's canon rule exists to prevent. Instead: (1) add a numbered Q to docs/15 stating the conflict in the two quotes above; (2) implement the proposed default behind a switch, which is the project's rule for an ambiguity — a `TRANSITION_MS` constant on ScreenRouter defaulting to 0 (today's behaviour, M5 intact) and a `_fade` path that, when non-zero, cross-fades the outgoing `_current` against the incoming Control over 110ms with `Tween.EASE_OUT` inside `_load_into_host` (ScreenRouter.gd:97-116) — no position change, so M5's 'no slide' holds literally; (3) gate it on `GameSettings.reduced_motion` (JUICE-06) and on the §12.1 budget of ≤140ms fully settled. WHAT A PERSON MUST DECIDE: whether a cross-dissolve counts as 'the desk moving'. It is a one-word answer and it unblocks JUICE-03 and the `ui.tab` hook's 'on first pixel of the dissolve' sync (docs/13 §12.4).

items.title: reduced_motion has exactly one consumer and no enforcement — every new tween in M6 will silently ignore it
items.evidence: `grep -rn reduced_motion --include=*.gd .` outside tests finds four lines: the default (game/core/GameSettings.gd:37), two Settings-screen strings (game/screens/Settings.gd:48, :72), and exactly ONE consumer — game/ui/SceneStage.gd:263, which stops the flame AnimatedSprites and `set_process(false)`. Settings.gd:48-51's own docstring confirms SceneStage is the only one: "SceneStage is their consumer". Meanwhile `grep -rn "create_tween|tween_property|AnimationPlayer" --include=*.gd game/` returns ZERO hits anywhere in the codebase — there is not one tween in the game today, which is why the gap has cost nothing yet. JUICE-02, JUICE-03 and JUICE-05 each add several.
items.risk: If this lands after JUICE-02/03/05 instead of before, the lint will fail against three fresh call sites and the loop will be tempted to weaken the lint. Sequence it first.
items.spec_source: docs/13 §13 (reduced motion row, reduced flashing row), §12.2 motion table
items.area: M6 polish — audio, juice, accessibility
items.remaining_work_note:
DONE, and built BEFORE the tweens exactly as the item asked — the codebase still contains zero `create_tween()` calls outside the one sanctioned helper, which is the only order in which a lint like this ever holds.

`GameSettings.motion_scale()` returns 0.0 or 1.0 and `motion_duration(ms, floor_ms := 0)` turns docs/13 §12.2's milliseconds into the seconds a Tween wants, applying the setting in one place. The zero is the design: a 0.0-duration tween completes on the next frame and still applies its final value, so a call site needs NO branch and reduced motion cannot become a second code path nobody exercises. `floor_ms` is §13's one carve-out — "Stamps still land (they carry state) but at 60ms with no rotation" — so `motion_duration(120, 60)` is 0.12 normally and 0.06 reduced, never nothing.

`Widgets.tween(node)` is the only door and `tools/lint_motion.sh` is the lock, wired into verify.sh's stage 0 beside the class_name lint and proven by reintroduction. It binds the Tween to the node so a screen's animation cannot outlive the screen, and refuses a node outside the tree rather than handing back something that fails later.

THE §13 FLASHING HALF TURNED OUT TO BE AN AMBIGUITY, filed as docs/15 BL-75. "No element exceeds 3 changes per second" read literally bans the shipped art: the hearth flames run at 9 fps, both arena fires at 8, the townsfolk idles at 5. The shipped reading is UI-only, and it is the doc set's own — §12.2 closes with "ambient motion belongs to the world layer and is doc 12's", which puts the flames outside §12's scope before §13 speaks, and a fire cycling through near-identical frames is not a "change" in the sense a photosensitivity rule means. Switched as `FLASH_RULE_COUNTS_WORLD_MOTION` with `flash_rule_applies_to(layer)` as the single place it is asked; both readings are under test, the literal one held as a MEASUREMENT of what it would cost rather than as an argument. Nothing in it weakens the guarantee: a player who needs the motion stopped turns on reduced motion and `SceneStage` halts the world layer outright, and a test pins that consumer because it is what makes the ruling safe.

Fifteen tests in tests/unit/test_motion.gd. 1536 tests, gate green.

LinkButton is never passed through `_button()` — Theme.gd:247-250 sets only `font_color`, `font_hover_color`, `font`, `font_size` — so a focused link shows NOTHING (its underline is `UNDERLINE_MODE_ON_HOVER`, game/ui/Widgets.gd:195-196, which is hover, not focus). items.title: Palette.band_color is a 3-step red/amber/green ramp — the exact axis docs/13 §8.3 rejects as CVD-unsafe — and no CVD verification exists anywhere
items.evidence: game/ui/Palette.gd:97-108: `band_color` returns `DANGER` (<30), `CAUTION` (<65), `POSITIVE` (>=65), where DANGER=`#F73526` red, CAUTION=`#FBB62B` amber, POSITIVE=`#32C24D` green (Palette.gd:71-73). docs/13 §8.3 (docs/13-ui-ux.md:312) rules directly against this: "**Why red→teal and not red→green:** ... The hue axis runs red → ochre → olive → teal, which stays separable under deuteranopia and protanopia; **a red→green ramp does not.** Verification is a blocking QA item in §13." docs/13 §13's CVD row is **Blocking: Yes**. docs/15 Q-79 (docs/15-open-questions.md:526) already proposed the fix: "the other seven interpolated along the L* ladder, high end shifted green→teal for CVD safety". The art pass then adopted the reference hues anyway — art/ref/specs/04-palette.md §5 and §7 — and its §7 contrast audit is WCAG-luminance only: "Computed for every text role × {panel, card, nav-active, slot} ... **No reference pairing fails AA for its size class**". There is no protanopia/deuteranopia/tritanopia/greyscale check in that spec or anywhere in tests/ (`grep -rln "contrast|greyscale|luminance" tests/` matches only test_raid_plan.gd and test_settings.gd, neither about colour). Compounding it, `POSITIVE #32C24D` and `CAUTION #FBB62B` are close in lightness, so §8.3's fallback channel — "Adjacent morale bands must remain distinguishable by lightness alone" — does not hold either.
items.remaining_work: This is a genuine standing conflict between two authorities, not an oversight: the reference concepts set the art bar and they paint red/amber/green, while docs/13 §13 makes CVD safety blocking. Apply the project's ambiguity rule rather than picking a side. (1) Add a numbered Q to docs/15 stating the conflict with the two quotes above and linking Q-79. (2) Put it behind a switch: keep `Palette.band_color` as the reference ramp (default), and add `Palette.band_color_cvd(value)` implementing §8.3's L*-ordered red→ochre→olive→teal, selected by a new `colourblind_safe` option. NOTE: docs/13 §15.1's rule is "if an option is not in this table, it does not exist in the settings screen", so the new key requires a row added to §15.1 FIRST — GameSettings.gd:29's own docstring says adding a key without adding the row "is the same mistake in the other direction". BACKLOG.md:169 already asks for "colourblind-safe morale coding", which is the mandate for the row. (3) Build the verification the docs call blocking: `tools/art/cvd.py` applying the Brettel/Viénot protanope, deuteranope and tritanope matrices plus a greyscale pass to a screenshot, wired the way tools/art/refdiff.py already is; and `tests/unit/test_palette_cvd.gd` asserting that adjacent bands in whichever ramp is active differ by ≥ 5 in L* AND by ≥ 3:1 after deuteranope simulation. WHAT A PERSON MUST DO: rule on whether the shipped hue ramp is the reference's three-step or §8.3's ten-step — this is exactly the 'where the reference concepts' UI does not fit the design, the design wins' judgement, and it changes the look of the most-read element in the game. The switch and the tooling can and should be built before that ruling; the default cannot be flipped without it.
items.risk: `band_color` also drives the success-chance readout (art/ref/specs/04-palette.md §5: "one function serves both"), so any change touches RaidPrep's figure as well as every morale chip. Keep the two callers separable before changing the ramp.

`tools/art/refdiff.py:119-121` computes ONE verdict for the whole framebuffer: `INDISTINGUISHABLE if iou > 0.80 and mae < 6 else VERY CLOSE if iou > 0.65 and mae < 14 else RECOGNISABLY THE SAME DESIGN if iou > 0.45 else DIFFERENT`. The stored measurements prove the whole-screen IoU is dominated by letterforms, not layout: `build/diff/kit_diff.json` mae 16.854 / layout_iou 0.2796; `build/diff/town_diff.json` 26.313 / 0.4113; `build/diff/raidprep_diff.json` 20.184 / **0.1744** — and raidprep is the one run WITH the scene masked out (tools/diff_all.sh:26 `--mask 210,77,928,640`), i.e. the chrome-only score is the worst of the three. Masking the picture and scoring only the typeset chrome makes the number go DOWN, which is only possible if the residual is glyph shape. IoU > 0.65 is therefore unreachable while the reference uses a different UI font, exactly as BACKLOG.md:135 concluded.

2026-09-11, concrete: Town's `layout_iou 0.44` was measured while its background was a crop of the very concept it was being scored against — the scene region was the grader's own pixels. On the bare plate the whole-screen number is 0.1029 masked / 0.1322 unmasked, and the chrome-only mae is 36.7. The verdict word did not change (DIFFERENT either way), which is the point: a single whole-screen verdict cannot tell 'the chrome drifted' from 'the art is deliberately new'.

items.title: Define and build the expand-mode wide-screen check
items.evidence: The switch exists and applies live: `game/core/GameSettings.gd:41` (`"display_aspect": "keep"`), `:209-213 apply_display_aspect()` sets `window.content_scale_aspect` to EXPAND or KEEP, `game/ui/Boot.gd:114-118` applies it at boot and `game/screens/Settings.gd:312-313` re-applies it without a rebuild. The layout cannot follow it: `game/ui/Frame.gd:250 relayout(p, size)` is fully size-aware (`:253 right = size.x - ...`, `:277 chip_host.position = Vector2(size.x - GUTTER - 1 - CHIPS_W, ...)`, `:289 sidebar_host`, `:296 strip.size = size.x - 30`) but `grep -rn 'resized|item_rect_changed' game/ --include=*.gd` returns exactly one hit — the COMMENT at Frame.gd:248 ("Screens call this from a `resized` handler"). No screen does. So toggling the setting at runtime widens the canvas and leaves every region at its 1536 rects. `art/ref/specs/11-godot-architecture.md:22` names the two failures that overturned expand as the default: "Concept 3's baked-in sidebar showed through beside ours" and "the strip's fixed-x panels stopped short of the edge".
items.remaining_work:
WHAT THE CHECK MUST ASSERT (four things, in this order):
(A) REFERENCE FRAMING IS UNCHANGED AT 1536. A pure unit test on Frame: `Frame.relayout(p, Vector2(1536,1024))` must reproduce spec 01 §1's measured rects exactly — header 0,0,1536,74; divider y=74 h=2; rail 0,77,207,640; scene 210,77,929,640; shared rule 0,717,1536,2; sidebar 1142,79,378,635; strip 13,734,1506,262; chip_host right edge = 1519. This is the regression guard that makes the rest safe.
(B) EVERY EDGE-ANCHORED REGION FOLLOWS THE WIDTH. `Frame.relayout(p, Vector2(1820,1024))` (1920/1080*1024 = 1820, the real 16:9 logical canvas from spec 11 §1) must give: header.size.x == divider.size.x == shared_rule.size.x == 1820; chip_host.position.x + Frame.CHIPS_W == 1820 - GUTTER - 1; sidebar_host.position.x + SIDEBAR_W == 1820 - GUTTER; strip.size.x == 1790; rail unchanged at 0,77,207,*; scene width grows by 284.
(C) RELAYOUT ACTUALLY RUNS. Wire it: in `Frame.build()` connect `p.root.resized` to a bound `relayout(p)`, and have `Settings.gd:312-313` call it after `apply_display_aspect`. Test: build a frame at 1536, set root.size to 1820, await one frame, assert (B)'s rects — this fails today because nothing reconnects.
(D) NO BARE GROUND AND NO FOREIGN PIXELS BESIDE THE PLATE. This is the failure spec 11 §1 recorded. The scene plates are fixed 1536-wide textures (`game/screens/Town.gd:117` SceneStage camp, `Guildhall.gd:123`, `Market.gd:139`, `Tavern.gd:100`, `RaidPrep.gd:131`, all STRETCH_KEEP), so at 1820 there is a 284px band with no art. Decide and assert one rule: the band is painted `Palette.GROUND_PAGE` and the plate is LEFT-anchored (or centred) — never scaled, never tiled. Pixel assertion via `tools/shot.gd`: shoot at 1820x1024 with `--fixture` and assert every pixel in the band x=1536..1819, y=77..716 equals GROUND_PAGE within tolerance 2, and that NO control's `global_position.x + size.x` exceeds 1820 (a button off the canvas still passes the string-walking tests but is unreachable by a player).
HOW TO RUN IT: `tools/shot.gd` already accepts an arbitrary WxH (tools/shot.gd:51-53) and pins a SubViewport of exactly that size, so add one target to `tools/diff_all.sh` — `res://game/screens/Town.tscn` at 1820x1024 — and score it NOT against a concept (sizes must match, refdiff.py:69 refuses a mismatch) but against the two mechanical assertions in (D). Record the outcome in `art/ref/specs/11-godot-architecture.md` §1 so the switch's cost is documented rather than rediscovered.
items.spec_source: art/ref/specs/11-godot-architecture.md §1 (keep vs expand, and the 1820x1024 logical canvas); art/ref/specs/01-concept1-home-layout.md §1 (the rects (A) pins)
items.risk: Connecting `resized` risks a relayout storm during window drags and a re-entrancy loop if a child's resize re-fires the parent's. Guard with a size-equality early-out at the top of relayout. Also: (A) must be written and green BEFORE (C) is wired, or a bug in the resize path silently moves the reference framing and the whole diff gate drifts with it.

items.title: Author the two crap trinkets from docs/09 §10.2 — not docs/10 §9.2's names or stats
items.evidence: `grep -rn 'Cracked Charm' data/ sim/ game/ tests/` returns nothing — neither trinket exists. Three docs currently name them differently: docs/10-content-and-encounters.md:434-435 proposes 'Trinket of Mild Competence / +1 Damage' and 'Trinket of Faint Encouragement / +1 AC'; docs/01 §8.2 proposes 'Trinket of Mild Competence — +1 Damage'; docs/09-items-and-itemization.md:539-540 gives 'Cracked Charm of Power / +1 Power' (Adventure 0) and 'Cracked Charm of Health / +2 HP' (Tutorial Raid). docs/09:541 settles ownership in terms: 'this doc owns item stat blocks, so this is the single pair … [01 §8.2]'s and [10 §9.2]'s … should cite the two rows above by name and stat rather than propose their own.' docs/11-economy-and-crafting.md:519 (Q5) and docs/15-open-questions.md:488 (Q-55) both confirm +1 Power, because docs/09 §12.2 restricts `damage` to weapons. data/items_starting.json is `tier: 0, source: "start"` with 22 items, which is where docs/09 §12 puts tutorial rewards ('`tier` 0 = starting gear and tutorial rewards').
items.risk: The tempting mistake is transcribing docs/10 §9.2 (the doc this slice is written against) instead of docs/09 §10.2 (the doc that owns item stat blocks and says so). '+1 Damage' is not expressible as a trinket row at all — docs/09 §12.2 restricts `damage` to weapons.

items.remaining_work_note:
DONE. `data/items_tutorial.json` carries docs/09 §10.2 G12's authored pair — Cracked Charm of Power (+1 Power) and Cracked Charm of Health (+2 HP) — mounted from `ContentDB.DEFAULT_PATHS` beside the tutorial encounters, because docs/10 §9 gives the whole game exactly two tutorial rungs and Tier 2 does not repeat them.

docs/09's stats, not docs/10 §9.2's: docs/09 owns item stat blocks and says so at §10.2, and docs/10's placeholder names a '+1 Damage' trinket, which cannot be expressed as an item row at all because docs/09 §12.2 restricts `damage` to weapons.

THE IDS MOVED AND docs/15 BL-77 RECORDS WHY. The shipped code named `ITM_T0_TUT_CRACKED_POWER` / `..._HEALTH`, which do not parse under docs/09 §12.1's grammar `ITM_T{tier}_{SOURCE}_{FAMILY}_{SLOT}` — and §12.1's SOURCE enumeration had no token for a tutorial reward even though the same table's tier row reads '0 = starting gear AND TUTORIAL REWARDS'. `TUT` was added to the doc; the ids are now `ITM_T0_TUT_UNIV_TRINKET_POWER` / `ITM_T0_TUT_UNIV_TRINKET_HEALTH`. `START` was the alternative and is wrong for a load-bearing reason: `source` is not a label in this codebase — Loot's non-raid pool selects on it, and `items_starting.json`'s `starting_sets` is what every new Common is dressed from.

`tests/unit/test_items_tutorial.gd` (8 tests) holds the grammar, the stat blocks, the unreachability from any rolled pool, the inequality against the LIVE Adventure charms rather than a copied number, and that `GameState.TUTORIAL_TRINKET`'s ids resolve — which is the assertion that was missing while the grant silently handed over nothing.

items.title: Loot: tutorials pay 0 gold and can drop nothing — add the payout rows and the guaranteed, once-only trinket
items.evidence: sim/core/Loot.gd:36 `const ADVENTURE_PAYOUT := {"A1": 4, "A2": 6, "A3": 10}` and :31 RAID_PAYOUT have no A0/TR row; `payout()` at :268-283 returns 0 for any slot in neither table, so both tutorials pay nothing. docs/11-economy-and-crafting.md:97 (F2) prices them: 'Adventure 0: 4 G · Tutorial Raid: 8 G'. `drop_pool()` at :96-110 filters the non-raid branch on `it.source == "adventure"`, and data/items_starting.json declares `"source": "start"`, so a tier-0 trinket can never enter the pool. `rolls_for()` at :71-79 would still return `loot_slots.size()` = 1 for a tutorial. The guaranteed-drop precedent already exists at :142-146 (`E5_GUARANTEES_TRINKET`). `roll_drops()` (:124) takes no clear count, so it cannot honour docs/10 §9.3's one-time rule on its own.
items.risk: Putting the once-only guard inside `Loot.roll_drops` would break its documented purity contract (sim/core/Loot.gd:17-19: 'Pure and deterministic. No Node, no global RNG') by making a drop depend on campaign state. Put the guard in GameState, where every other campaign consequence already lives (docs/14 §3.1).
items.area: M5 tutorials — Adventure 0 and the Tutorial Raid (docs/10 §9)
items.remaining_work_note:
DONE, and half of it turned out to be built already. `GameState._grant_tutorial_trinket`, its once-only guard and the bypass that keeps `Loot.roll_drops` out of the tutorial path had all shipped — against two item ids that resolved to null, so a first clear granted NOTHING and the test branched on whether the rows existed rather than failing. M5-TUT-04 authored the rows.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY MISSING: the gold. docs/11 §F2 prices the pair in one line — 'Adventure 0: 4 G · Tutorial Raid: 8 G' — and neither slot was in RAID_PAYOUT or ADVENTURE_PAYOUT, so `payout()` took its unknown-rung branch and answered 0 for both. `TUTORIAL_PAYOUT` is that row, consulted first, and §F5's repeat decay applies unchanged because docs/10 §9.3 keeps a resolved tutorial 'replayable for gold' while the trinket is gone.

That constant is ALSO the tutorial test inside the file: `payout`, `rolls_for` and `drop_pool` all branch on `is_tutorial_slot`, which reads it, so a tutorial is exactly the set of slots priced as one and there is no second list to fall out of step with.

`rolls_for` returns 0 and `drop_pool` returns empty for a tutorial, explicitly rather than by accident. GameState already bypassed the roll; the bypass having a second author in the pure layer means a future caller cannot reintroduce the hazard docs/10 §9.2 names — the non-raid pool would otherwise map the declared 'trinket' loot slot to Slot.TRINKET and hand a tutorial Adventure's own charms (+7 HP, +2 Power), the very items the crap pair must be worse than.

Three new tests in `test_loot.gd` and `test_tutorials.gd`; the conditional one is deleted, because a test that passes either way is not a gate.

items.title: tanks_required: 0 silently becomes 2, and two docs disagree on Adventure 0's tank count
items.evidence:
VERIFIED AGAINST THE TREE 2026-09-11 — THE EVIDENCE BELOW IS STALE. (reconciliation sweep: one agent read this entry and the files it names, and every claim of 'done' was then put to two independent skeptics whose brief was to refute it. Four survived the read and did not survive the refutation.)
Specifically no longer true: "game/core/RaidPlan.gd:96-99 `static func tanks_required(encounter) -> int: if encounter != null and encounter.tanks_required > 0: return encounter.tanks_required; return DEFAULT_TANKS_REQUIRED` — an authored 0 is indistinguishable from an absent field and resolves to 2."
What the tree actually shows now:
  - (b) TRAP CLOSED AND ARMED: sim/model/Encounter.gd:268-271 `if e.tanks_required <= 0:` appends "%s: tanks_required %d — the ruling is default 2, tutorials 1; 0 reads as 'absent' downstream and silently becomes 2", inside from_dict's structural block, with a 7-line comment at :261-267 explaining why the validator was chosen over loosening the guard.
  - THE VALIDATOR IS ACTUALLY REACHED (not a dead errors array): sim/content/ContentDB.gd:503-508 `_load_encounters` calls `Encounter.from_dict(raw, errs)` and forwards every entry to `_err()`, and `is_valid()` at ContentDB.gd:172 returns `errors.is_empty()` — so an authored 0 now fails content load rather than resolving to 2.
  - CHEAP-BRANCH CONSEQUENCE HELD CONSISTENT: game/core/RaidPlan.gd:97-100 `tanks_required()` still reads `if encounter != null and encounter.tanks_required > 0` with `DEFAULT_TANKS_REQUIRED := 2` at RaidPlan.gd:25, and sim/model/Encounter.gd:192 still defaults an absent key to 2 — i.e. the risk named in the entry (guard loosened to `>= 0` without changing the default) was correctly avoided. Callers exist: RaidPlan.gd:270 (`var required := tanks_required(encounter)`) and RaidPlan.gd:455 (the suggest_party role quota).
  - (a) DOC CONFLICT RESOLVED IN DATA: data/encounters_tutorial_t1.json:27 (`t1_tut_a0`, slot A0, party_size 4) and :58 (`t1_tut_tr`, slot TR, party_size 6) both carry `"tanks_required": 1`; the `_notes` array carries the departure note "TANKS REQUIRED 1, NOT docs/10 §9.1's 'no tanks required'", citing docs/15's per-fight tank ruling by its source chain (docs/06 Q6/Q7, docs/07 OQ-3) — that is Q-47 at docs/15-open-questions.md:523, though the note names the ruling rather than the literal label "Q-47".
  - TESTED, HALF (b): tests/unit/test_encounters.gd:280-290 `test_validator_refuses_a_zero_tank_requirement` asserts `_complains_about({"tanks_required": 0}, "tanks_required")` and `-1` are refused, and that `1` and an absent key are not — via the real `_errors_for`/`Encounter.from_dict` helper at test_encounters.gd:246-255.
  - TESTED, HALF (a): tests/unit/test_tutorials.gd:71-79 `test_party_sizes_and_tank_counts` asserts `_tut("A0").party_size == 4`, `_tut("TR").party_size == 6`, `_tut("A0").tanks_required == 1`, `_tut("TR").tanks_required == 1`, with the Q-47-over-docs/10 tie-break written into the comment.
  - THE ONE MISSING ACCEPTANCE ASSERTION: no test anywhere asserts `RaidPlan.tanks_required(<tutorial>) == 1`. tests/unit/test_raid_plan.gd contains no call to `RaidPlan.tanks_required` at all — its only tank line is :93 `assert_eq(int(a["tanks_required"]), 2)` on a Raid-1 analysis dict. The seam is exercised but never pinned: tests/unit/test_ladder.gd:159 asserts only the inequality `tanks >= RaidPlan.tanks_required(tr)`, and tests/unit/test_tutorials.gd:208 uses `RaidPlan.tanks_required(enc)` as a party-shaping input inside `_premade()`, where a regression to 2 would not fail an assert.
  - build/plan/handoff-tutorials.md:139-150 (H5) is the implementing agent's own note and matches the tree: it states the validator half was done and that `tests/unit/test_raid_plan.gd` "should gain `RaidPlan.tanks_required(a0) == 1` and `(tr) == 1`" — still owed.
  - docs/10-content-and-encounters.md:419 still prints Adventure 0 as "4, pre-made, no tanks required" — not a defect against this item (remaining_work asked only for the cited `_notes` departure, not a docs/10 edit), but the doc text itself is unchanged. build/plan/q-tutorials.md:66-78 records the ruling as DECIDED — refused at load.

ORIGINAL EVIDENCE, kept as the record of why this was filed:
sim/model/Encounter.gd:151 defaults `tanks_required` to 2 when the key is absent. game/core/RaidPlan.gd:96-99 `static func tanks_required(encounter) -> int: if encounter != null and encounter.tanks_required > 0: return encounter.tanks_required; return DEFAULT_TANKS_REQUIRED` — an authored 0 is indistinguishable from an absent field and resolves to 2. docs/10-content-and-encounters.md:417 says Adventure 0 fields '4, pre-made, **no tanks required**'; docs/15-open-questions.md:480 (Q-47) rules 'Per-fight `tanks_required` (default 2, **tutorials 1**)'.

- sim/model/Encounter.gd:268-271 still refuses `tanks_required <= 0` at load; tests/unit/test_encounters.gd:286-289 still pins 0 and -1 refused, 1 and absent accepted
- data/encounters_tutorial_t1.json:27 and :58 both `"tanks_required": 1`; :10 `_notes` departure note citing docs/15's per-fight ruling; tests/unit/test_tutorials.gd:78-79 pin the data

`tools/playtest.gd` plays the whole Tier 1 campaign headlessly, eight guilds by default, driving the campaign and not the UI. The ladder and the party suggestion were EXTRACTED from the screens into `RaidPlan` first — `ladder()`, `locked_reason()`, `next_open_mission()`, `suggest_party()` — because a harness that walked its own ladder or chalked its own twelve would prove a campaign nobody plays is completable. AdventureBoard and RaidPrep now call those, 49 lines of duplicated rule were deleted from RaidPrep, and 12 tests in tests/unit/test_ladder.gd hold the shared rules.

The simulated player is deliberately the FLOOR: it takes the board's own suggestion every time, never reorders the chalked party, never holds loot back, never farms a cleared rung. It does skip a tutorial it cannot beat after five attempts — canon offers that door in terms and docs/15 Q-90 makes it permanent — and the skip is reported as a WALL so using an escape hatch is never mistaken for the rung being fine.

Both bounds are derived, not picked: the per-rung patience is docs/15 Q-90's own upper bound ("3-5 attempts ... for a first Raid 1 clear"), and the day cap is that times the ladder's own length times the most days one attempt can cost — a Day Tick plus docs/02 §4.3's slowest possible recovery, which `GameState.REST_DAY_LIMIT`'s comment already records as 40.

WIRED INTO verify.sh AS STAGE 6/7, AS A WARNING RATHER THAN A FAILURE, and that is temporary and written down in the stage itself: the first run found a real wall (M6-BAL-04) and making the stage fail today would make the gate permanently red and stop every other piece of work. The `WARN` prints the wall summary on every full gate run so it cannot be forgotten. When M6-BAL-04 is answered, the warning becomes a failure and the comment comes out with it.

What canon DOES publish is target *rounds* per boss (docs/08 §9.2, reproduced in docs/10 §5.4's escalation table: E1..E5 at 1..5 stars) and a star ramp (docs/01:90-93). `tools/balance_sweep.gd:31-33`'s three bounds are explicitly self-described as "deliberately loose... a smoke test for 'the game is still playable', not a tuning assertion". On scope: only Tier 1 exists — `ls data/` shows `encounters_t1.json` and `encounters_adventure_t1.json` and nothing else; BACKLOG.md's M5 section still has "Raids 2-5 + Adventures 2-5 encounter definitions" and "Tier scaling generator" unchecked, and BUILD_STATE.md:37 names "Content is Tier 1 only" as one of the three biggest gaps.
items.remaining_work: A person must supply two things before this item is workable. FIRST, the designer must sign off a target clear-rate curve: the shape of the ask is one clear rate per encounter per gear-stage-at-attempt (the stage docs/08 §9.2 says the boss is actually fought in — "the boss is fought in the gear the boss before it dropped"), plus a tolerance band. The loop can and should PREPARE this rather than wait idle: write a 🔷 PROPOSED curve into a new `docs/15-open-questions.md` entry derived from what canon already fixes — the 1-to-5-star ramp (docs/01:90-93), docs/08 §9.2's per-boss target_rounds, and docs/03 §6.4's nineteen-row pacing table (already reproduced row-for-row by `sim/core/Reputation.gd`, which makes it the closest thing canon has to an intended attempt count per rung) — state the derivation, and mark it as needing sign-off in the same register as Q-53 and RC-8. It must NOT be tuned into the game as though canon had specified it; Q-29 is already on record (BUILD_STATE.md:47) as "the one balance value changed on judgement alone" and the bar is that there is only one. SECOND, 'across all tiers' is blocked on M5: Tiers 2-5 do not exist, so the honest scope of an M6 balance pass today is Tier 1 (A1-A3, E1-E5) only. Split the backlog line into two: 'Balance pass 2, Tier 1, against the signed-off curve' (doable once the curve exists and M6-BAL-01/02 land) and 'Full-ladder balance pass, Tiers 1-5' (docs/16 W3.11, sized L, blocked on M5). Note also that Q-22 (docs/15:2075, morale-vs-rarity dominance) is explicitly held OPEN pending a re-measurement at Tier 2 — it must not be closed by a Tier 1 pass.

items.title: Save-format freeze + migration test — the chain exists and is walked, but no migration has ever run and no fixture save is committed
items.evidence: `game/core/SaveGame.gd` implements docs/14 §7 properly: atomic temp+rename write (`write_to`), header-first read (`read_header`, line 169-ish), refusal of a newer save before anything is built (`incompatibility`), `.bak` before migrating (`_write_backup`), and a real-but-empty chain — `const MIGRATIONS := {}` at line 66, walked one step at a time by `migrate()`. But `const OLDEST_MIGRATABLE := 10` (line 61) equals `GameState.SAVE_VERSION := 10` (game/core/GameState.gd:46), so no migration path is reachable, and the test that would prove the `.bak` rule takes an early return: `tests/unit/test_savegame.gd:200-203` — `if SaveGame.OLDEST_MIGRATABLE >= GameStateScript.SAVE_VERSION: assert_eq(...); return`. docs/14:768 (§7.3 non-negotiable 2) requires "Every migration gets a test with a committed fixture save at the old version (tests/data/saves/v7_sample.json)" — `ls tests/data` -> "No such file or directory". `CONTENT_VERSION := 1` (line 55) is written into every header but nothing reads it back: there is no `reconcile_content` (docs/14 §7.3's row for a content id that no longer exists) anywhere in the tree.
items.spec_source: docs/14 §7.1-§7.3 (header, atomic write, versioning and migration, the three non-negotiables at :765-770); docs/15 Q-55 (why the header lives inside one JSON document) and Q-56 (why SAVE_DIR is a variable)
items.risk: Two traps. First, `tests/run_tests.gd:11-13` sets `SaveGame.SAVE_DIR = "user://test_saves"` and purges it — a fixture read from `res://tests/data/saves/` must be read by path, not through `slot_path()`, or the test will look in the redirected directory and find nothing. Second, bumping `SAVE_VERSION` invalidates any dev's in-flight guild; that is exactly what the migration is for, so ship the migration and the bump in one commit, never the bump alone.

items.remaining_work_note:
DONE 2026-09-11. The grid FITS instead of scrolling: more than six dead switches the cell from 92px/44px-portrait to 60px/36px at a 4px separation, which is exactly six to a row (6x60 + 5x4 = 380 against LEFT_COL_W 392; a seventh would need 448), so twelve casualties are TWO rows instead of three and every name and class stays whole. The label also became two lines — name over class — because 'name — class' does not fit a compact cell and a wrapped em dash reads as a typo.

Scrolling was already in place and was not the fix: the column does scroll, so the overflow was hidden rather than legible, with no scrollbar to say so. That is why this was worth fixing by FITTING.

The metrics are static (`Results.fallen_metrics()` / `fallen_gap()`) and tests/unit/test_results_screen.gd holds the arithmetic against the column: six fit, seven do not, four roomy cells fit, five do not, and a full wipe's two rows fit the height the panel leaves under the headline and the tally. Checked on a 1536x1024 shot with the raid fixture's 12-of-12 wipe.

items.title: docs/14 §10.1 gate 2 — nothing asserts that re-running the content generator leaves data/ unchanged
items.spec_source: docs/14 §10.1 pre-export gate (2), 'gen_items.gd produces no tree change'; docs/15 BL-74 records it as the one gate of six still owed
items.evidence: `tools/gen_items.gd` exists and wrote the 412 records in data/items_t2..t5_*.json (docs/15 BL-69, BL-70). `tests/unit/test_gen_items_merge.gd` covers the hand-authored merge and `test_tier_budget.gd` the budget, but nothing runs the generator and compares its output to what is committed — so a hand edit to a generated row, or a generator change that was never re-run, is invisible until somebody regenerates and sees a diff they did not expect.
items.remaining_work_note:
DONE, and it turned out to need no new checker. `tools/gen_items.gd` has had a `-- check` mode since the day it was written: it rebuilds all sixteen Tier 2-5 files in memory, compares them to what is committed, writes nothing, and exits non-zero naming any file that differs. It had NO CALLER for as long — which is the same shape as the defect M5-QAB-6 fixed, an instrument built and never wired.

So neither of the audit's two proposed shapes was the answer. Option (a) wanted an output-root override the generator does not have; option (b) wanted a unit test that re-derives the records, which would have been a SECOND implementation of the generator competing with the first. The existing mode compares the whole corpus against the real thing and is strictly better than either.

Wired as `tools/verify.sh` stage 2/8, right after the parse check, because it is as cheap as one and it guards data the tests below it read. Deliberately NOT in `tools/export_build.sh`: a release build that mutates the tree it is packing is worse than the gap, and `test_the_release_export_does_not_regenerate_anything` asserts it stays out.

PROVEN BY REINTRODUCTION, which is this project's bar: adding 7 to one `ac` in data/items_t3_raid.json turns the gate red and names the file; re-running the generator turns it green. Three tests in tests/unit/test_gen_items_merge.gd guard the wiring itself — that verify.sh really calls it, that export_build.sh really does not, and that every generated file declares its generator and names `hand_authored` as the one sanctioned way to keep an edit.

One note in the generated files had to change with it. It read "a hand edit here is lost on the next regeneration and nothing will warn you" — true when it was written, false from this commit, and a file that tells a reader the wrong thing about its own gate is worse than one that says nothing. All eight item files were regenerated to carry the corrected note; the diff is that note and nothing else. docs/15 BL-74's gate table and docs/14 §10.1 both now say all six pre-export gates run.
items.risk: The generated tiers do not SHIP until they are named (docs/15 BL-69), so this protects reviewability rather than a live game — but it is the gate that stops the tier work drifting away from its own generator while nobody is looking.

items.title: Seven dead build/plan/*.md citations in shipped code, and no lint watches that directory
items.spec_source: the same premise as tests/unit/test_docs_links.gd — 37 guessed doc slugs and 91 dead links survived four milestones because nothing checked
items.evidence: `grep -rnoE 'build/plan/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+\.md' sim/ game/ tests/ tools/ docs/ data/` yields 26 distinct targets, of which SEVEN do not exist: handoff-debt.md (sim/core/Recruitment.gd:375, sim/core/Reputation.gd:650), handoff-m5-endgame.md (sim/core/Achievements.gd:387 and :965, data/achievements.json:8 and :300), handoff-ship.md (tools/balance_sweep.gd:59), q-m5-endgame.md (data/achievements.json:10, :13, :222), q-saves.md (game/core/SaveGame.gd:71, game/screens/LoadSave.gd:8, game/screens/Settings.gd:437, tests/unit/test_loadsave_screen.gd:344), q-tank-swap.md (sim/core/RaidSim.gd:98), q-tiers.md (sim/content/TierScaling.gd:32). The eighth, q-ship.md, was repointed at docs/15 BL-74 this iteration. `tests/unit/test_docs_links.gd` walks docs/ and art/ref/specs/ only, so build/plan/ — the directory the parallel agent waves wrote their handoffs into and then consolidated away — is watched by nothing.
items.remaining_work_note:
DONE. Thirteen citation sites across nine files repointed, and the class of rot is now gated.

WHERE EACH WENT, and each was decided by reading the citing comment and the candidate rather than by matching a filename: handoff-debt.md (Recruitment.gd, Reputation.gd) -> audit M3-TUNE-04, which owns exactly the edits it described — `build/plan/report-debt.md` exists but is a different document and carries no §1, so that handoff was never written at all and the work behind it sat untracked for four milestones. handoff-m5-endgame.md split in two: the `record_attempt` hook LANDED (docs/15 BL-73) so Achievements.gd now cites the caller, and the lifetime counters did NOT, so they cite audit M5-QAB-5. handoff-ship.md (balance_sweep.gd) -> audit M6-BAL-01, the same gap read from the other end. q-m5-endgame.md (data/achievements.json x4) -> M5-QAB-4, M5-COMEDY-12 and M5-QAB-5. q-saves.md (x4) and q-tank-swap.md and q-tiers.md had no surviving home at all, so each comment now SAYS the write-up was lost and names what is missing — docs/13 §5 still has no row for the save screen (M3-SAVE-04 owns it, BL-73 is the precedent for propagating one), and the two switched ambiguities have no docs/15 row yet but both readings stay under test and neither ships until the tiers are named (BL-69).

THE LINT: `tests/unit/test_docs_links.gd` gained a fourth failure mode — every `build/plan/<name>.md` named from sim/, game/, tests/, tools/, data/ or the docs must resolve on disk. It carries an empty `PLAN_FILES_ALLOWED_TO_BE_MISSING` and the comment says it should stay empty, because 'it will exist soon' is precisely how eight dead citations were born. Verified by reintroducing one: the suite goes red and names the file and line.

Two of the repoints were written as historical notes that still named the dead file; those were reworded to keep the record ('a `build/plan/` handoff that was never written') without keeping the path, because a lint needing an exception for the comment explaining the exception is a lint with a hole in it.

FOUND WHILE DOING IT, filed as M5-QAB-6: `Achievements.evaluate()` has no caller anywhere. 1470 tests, gate green.
items.risk: Low to break, easy to do badly: a citation repointed at the wrong file is worse than a dead one, because a dead link announces itself and a wrong one does not. Each of the seven needs its citing comment read first.

items.title: The achievement engine has no caller — nothing evaluates, nothing is stored, and every record reads Locked forever
items.spec_source: docs/02 §4.4 (the ~40-entry record wall); docs/11 §11.1-§11.2 (the five types and their rewards); docs/10 §13 row 2, which makes achievement completion one third of the post-clear activity
items.evidence: `grep -rn 'Achievements.evaluate\|claim_grant' game/ sim/ --include=*.gd` returns NOTHING outside sim/core/Achievements.gd itself. `grep -n 'achievements_earned\|achievements_claimed' game/core/GameState.gd` returns nothing either — the two fields `Achievements.snapshot()` reads at lines 435-439 do not exist on GameState, so `_prop()` hands back its `{}` / `[]` fallbacks on every call. The consequences, in order of visibility: `state_of()` returns LOCKED for all 40 records, so the Records tab (game/screens/Guildhall.gd:292) is a wall of Locked rows that can never change; `earned_count()` is 0 forever, so the meter S17 and the Adventure's Board print reads 'Records 0 of 40' for a guild that has cleared everything; and no reward — coin, furnishing, reputation, town flag or consumables — has ever been paid. The 988-line engine, its 40 validated records and the whole reward-cap model are load-bearing for nothing. M5-QAB-1 is marked done for 'the record_attempt hook', but the hook that landed is the COMPLETION beat (M5-END-1, docs/15 BL-73), which calls `is_completion_encounter()` and not the evaluator.
items.remaining_work_note:
DONE, all three pieces in one commit as the item required.

STATE: `achievements_earned` (id -> the DAY it was earned, because that is the one part a snapshot cannot recompute and docs/02 §4.4 wants a wall you can read), `achievements_claimed`, and `town_flags` — the last is separate from `flags` on purpose: that is docs/14 §5.2's BUILD flag registry and `set_flag()` refuses an id it does not declare, so routing a statue through it would have let a reward switch the Blacksmith on. SAVE_VERSION 15 -> 16 with all four parts.

EVALUATION: `check_achievements(event)` unions `Achievements.evaluate()` into the earned set and emits the ids. Two call sites and the split between them is the design. `record_attempt()` passes the attempt as an event — the ONLY moment `EVENT_ONLY_KINDS` can be decided, because 'cleared it with nobody dead' is not a fact a save can rediscover. `autosave()` calls it eventless, and that is deliberate rather than a side effect smuggled into a save: docs/14 §7.4's list of save points IS the set of moments this campaign considers state-worthy, which is exactly the set of moments a snapshot record can newly become true — so a new record kind needs no new call site, and running before the write means what was just earned is in the file. The wall is stamped with the day the ATTEMPT happened, not the day the check runs: an attempt is a Day Tick (docs/05 §7) so the clock has already moved, and a wall saying the guild cleared Adventure 0 on day 43 when the raid was day 42 is wrong in the one field it is read for.

CLAIM: `claim_achievement()` is the hand docs/14 OQ-10 always described and `Achievements.claim_grant()`'s own comment already named. It applies all five reward kinds and refuses in the board's own sentence. The Records tab gained the control that `Guildhall.gd:94` had a field and a comment for and no button.

ONE DESIGN DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED WHILE WIRING IT: board coin paid through `add_gold()` would have fed `gold_earned_lifetime`, and the coin cap is 15% OF that — a faucet that widens itself every time it pays, which is precisely the substitution docs/11 §11.2 forbids. `add_gold()` grew a `counts_as_income` parameter and the claim passes false. `test_board_coin_is_gold_but_not_income` pins it.

22 tests: 19 in the new tests/unit/test_achievement_board.gd (the wire, the event-only half, the save, the five reward kinds, the cap) and three in test_screens.gd (the claim control appears only when earned, a locked row still prints its prize, and the refusal is printed where the press was). 1502 tests, all six gate stages green.
items.risk: It is a save-format change, so it costs the full four-part discipline. The reward side also touches the economy: docs/11 §11.2's caps are a share of lifetime income, and the counters that denominator needs do not exist either (M5-QAB-5) — land that first or the caps compute against zero and every claim is refused.
items.area: M5 — quest/achievement board and the endgame after Raid 5

items.title: A new guild is pinned at morale 45 by canon and the Adventure ladder is a wall there — 6 of 8 guilds stop at A2
items.spec_source: docs/05 §7.5 (baseline = 50 + rarity + facility + backstory) and §8's table (Common 45 at tier-0 facilities); docs/05 §8's drift rule, which stops dead at the baseline; docs/02 §4.3 (the rest worked example); docs/03 §6.4 (the pacing this is measured against); docs/11 §8.2 (what a facility costs)
items.evidence:
MEASURED by tools/playtest.gd, eight seeds, on the shipped tree: 0 of 8 guilds clear Tier 1. Six stop at A2 and two at A1, every one of them in full Tier 1 Adventure gear (`gear_label` reads T1A) at exactly 45 mean party morale, after 5 attempts — docs/15 Q-90's own upper bound for a first clear. The 45 is not bad luck, it is the ceiling: a new guild's twelve are all Common, `Morale.baseline_for(COMMON, facility_bonus=0)` is docs/05 §8's 45, `is_recovered()` defines recovered as at-or-above the baseline because §8's drift 'pulls toward the baseline and stops dead there', so `rest_until_recovered()` cannot ever return a roster above 45 for a facility-tier-0 guild. And tools/balance_sweep.gd's own lever readout says morale moves clear rate by 100 percentage points while rarity moves it by 13 — morale is THE lever, and canon pins the starting guild at the bottom of it.

The loop closes on gold: across ~100 days the eight guilds end on 60-64 G, having started with docs/01 §8.0's 60. No clears means no loot to sell and no reputation, so the guild cannot buy the Guildhall upgrade or the comfort items that are the only two things that raise the baseline — and it cannot clear the content that would pay for them. It is not a wall in one encounter; it is a closed circuit.

SHARPENED BY M6-BAL-01, which built docs/08 §9.1a's two intermediate gear stages so the sweep could finally meet each Adventure rung at the stage it is sized for. Measured, Common party, at the rung's own stage: A1 clears 50% at morale 55 and 0% at morale 15; A2 clears 63% at 55 and 0% at 15; A3 clears 0% at every morale (25% at Rare/55, 100% at Legendary). The ladder is passable at 55 and impassable at 15, and the ceiling canon gives a new guild is 45 — the cliff runs straight through the only morale a starting roster can reach. That is the number a ruling has to move, and it is now printed by `tools/verify.sh` stage 6/8 on every run.
items.remaining_work: A designer picks which lever moves, and every option changes a shipped number, which is why no build loop may take it. The measured options, costed: (a) RAISE THE COMMON BASELINE — docs/05 §7.5's `50 + rarity_offset`, where Common's offset is -5; moving it changes every band reading in docs/05 §8 and the morale history's whole scale. (b) MAKE THE FIRST FACILITY REACHABLE — docs/11 §8.2 prices the Guildhall upgrade and docs/01 §8.0 fixes the opening purse at 60 G; a starting guild that could afford tier 1 immediately would start at the baseline the ladder appears to be sized for. (c) SIZE A1-A3 FOR 45 — docs/10 §3 sized the Adventures, and docs/08 §9's budget is the instrument; this is the option that admits the on-ramp was costed against a morale the player cannot reach. (d) PAY MORALE FOR A WIPE DIFFERENTLY — docs/05 §7's wipe delta is what drags the roster to the floor between attempts. Do NOT split the difference and do not let the harness soften anything to go green; record the ruling in docs/15 and re-run tools/playtest.gd, which is now the instrument that says whether it worked.
items.risk: This is the third pinned balance defect and the largest: A3's 0/24 and the Tutorial Raid's 0/20 are single encounters, and this is the on-ramp the whole campaign stands on. It is also the first one measured end to end rather than encounter by encounter, which is why it was invisible until now — every individual part passes its own test.

items.title: The wipe sequence's two art beats — the ink bleed and the wax seal — have no assets
items.evidence:
As found (2026-09-11): `ls game/assets/ui/ | grep -iE 'seal|blot|stamp|wax'` returned nothing, and RaidView.gd's `_wipe_stamp()` / `_wipe_dim_page()` carried a comment saying each beat shipped without its texture. The press, the dim and the focus hand-off were pure code (M6-JUICE-03); these two were the remainder.

2026-09-15 (W4-HYGIENE, art overhaul wave 4 — read against the tree): both assets exist and are wired: game/assets/ui/wipe_blot.png (320x150) and game/assets/ui/wax_seal.png (72x72), generated by tools/aseprite/gen_wipe.lua (sources art/src/ui/, byte-checked by `build_art.sh --check`, verify stage 2b), loaded at RaidView.gd:273 `WIPE_BLOT` / :279 `WAX_SEAL` and placed by `_bleed_under()` / `_drop_seal()`; test_wipe_sequence.gd asserts both paths resolve. The RaidView docstrings that still said the blot was 'art that does not exist' / 'has no blot' after this item closed (RULES-04, COMBAT-21) were rewritten by W3-RAIDVIEW2 (RaidView.gd:242-247 names both PNGs and the generator), and test_project_hygiene.gd's LIES table now pins both phrases against wipe_blot.png.
items.remaining_work_note:
DONE. `tools/aseprite/gen_wipe.lua` authors both through the existing pipeline and writes the `.aseprite` source beside the PNG, which is what `build_art.sh` treats as the source of truth.

NEITHER COLOUR IS A NEW ONE, which was this item's stated trap. The blot is `Palette.DANGER` — the ink `Widgets.stamp()` already uses, so the bleed is the same substance as the word it spreads from. The seal is `CTA_TOP`/`CTA_BOTTOM` with the CTA plate's own bronze lip and near-black outline, because the commit control is the thing this project already calls wax (`Widgets.wax_button()`) and a seal in a second wax would say the two are unrelated materials.

Both are deterministic: no `math.random`, so the blot's irregularity is a fixed lobe table plus a two-frequency sine wobble on the radius. An ink blot that differed every build would show up as a diff nobody made, and `build_art.sh`'s staleness manifest would stop meaning anything.

The first render splashed rather than bled — a tight 9px fade and a high-frequency rim read as a splat, which is a different event and the wrong one for a sequence about a page being filed. Widened to 18px and halved the wobble; verified by compositing both textures over the chrome ground and looking.

Wired as the two beats they belong to: the bleed is added BEFORE the stamp box so sibling order puts the ink under the word (ink over it would read as a smear on the lens), fading in over docs/13 §11.4's 400ms; the seal drops into the lower-right at t=1,400 with a short settle. Neither takes §13's stamp floor, because §13 gives the floor to the stamp alone and names the bleed among the things reduced motion turns off — a test asserts exactly that asymmetry. Both beats skip silently if their texture is missing, so a stripped build still plays the sequence.

Five tests: the textures resolve, the duration is the doc's, the bleed has no floor while the stamp does, the seal lands past both mid-lines of the frame, and the ink is drawn under the word.
items.spec_source: docs/13 §11.4 (the t=900 ink bleed and the t=1,400 wax seal); docs/12 §7 (the Aseprite pipeline that would author them)
items.risk: Low. Both are decorative: the sequence reads correctly without them, which is why they were split out rather than blocking it. The only trap is authoring a second wax that does not match `ButtonWax` — the kit already committed to a material and a second one would read as a different game.

items.title: The audit queue goes stale silently, and the loop pays for it in orientation every iteration
items.spec_source: build/plan/loop-brief.md step 1 ('orient from files, never from recollection') — which only holds while the files are true
items.evidence: Thirteen open items were found finished in one week: M6-BAL-01, M6-EXP-06, M6-A11Y-03, M6-A11Y-08, half of M6-A11Y-04, M5-COMEDY-06, m5-m02-raid-wide-ac, M6-DOC-01, M6-A11Y-02, Q59-0, M5-TUT-07, M3-SAVE-05 and DW-B2. Every one had been completed inside some other item's work and nobody walked back to the plan. Twice the staleness cost the PICK rather than only the orientation: two consecutive iterations chose an item, read the file, and found the work already done.
items.remaining_work_note:
DONE. `tools/audit_stale.py` ranks every open item by how much of what it NAMES already exists in the tree — the functions it says are missing, the constants it says are owed, the files it says do not exist. That is the shape all thirteen had, and ranking by it puts them at the top of a list instead of in the twentieth iteration's way.

IT IS A DETECTOR AND NOT A JUDGE, and its header says so: the false positive is an item whose PREMISE is that a symbol exists but nothing calls it — M6-JUICE-08, filed the same day, scores 5 of 5 and is genuinely open. Every hit needs its citing sentence read. It closes nothing and edits nothing.

`tests/unit/test_audit_hygiene.gd` holds the invariants that keep the queue's shape readable: unique ids, a status the brief can act on, an open item that says what is left, a done item that says what it did and owes nothing, a blocked item that says what a person must decide, and a `spec_source` on everything — because an item with no source is an instruction with no authority. It deliberately does NOT assert that no item is stale: staleness is a judgement about the tree rather than a property of the file, and a test that tried would either be the detector or a lie.

Six items closed in this pass on top of the seven already found by hand.
items.risk: The detector is a heuristic and will always have false positives; the mitigation is that it says so loudly and closes nothing itself. The real risk is the opposite — that a future iteration trusts its ranking and closes an item without reading it.

items.title: Four ambient/action mistake types have a name and no consequence: AFK, LOOT_CALL, ARGUMENT, NO_CONSUMABLE
items.spec_source: docs/07 §5.5 / §10 (the ambient types and their described consequences); build/plan/ship/SIM.md SIM-15; build/plan/ship/00-plan.md §2 W7-SIM-EFFECTS
items.evidence: Filed 2026-09-15 (W6-LEDGER, from SIM-15): `MIS_AFK` causes no 1-3 round absence, `MIS_LOOT_CALL` skips no action and flags no morale, `MIS_ARGUMENT` names no second raider and carries no rest-of-encounter penalty, `MIS_NO_CONSUMABLE` leaves the buff applied. Each fires, prints its line, and changes nothing. (The fifth type SIM-15 lists, NINJAPULL, is unreachable by construction — CONTENT-12 — and is retired rather than given an effect: ship plan §6 #58.)
items.remaining_work: In W7-SIM-EFFECTS's one regeneration: AFK = the raider skips the next 1-3 actions (a token with a duration, drawn on the mistake's own channel); LOOT_CALL = the current action is skipped and the event carries a morale note; ARGUMENT = a second living raider is named in the event (`caused_by` shape) and both take a small `situational_bp` penalty for the rest of the encounter; NO_CONSUMABLE = the pre-fight buff the raider carried is stripped at the mistake. Each lands through the existing `_apply_mistake` seam, is written up as one docs/15 BL row, and the goldens regenerate once for the wave (ship plan §0.2). Add `test_raid_sim.gd` cases per type asserting the consequence, not only the line.
items.risk: Every consequence moves the sweep. Land in the wave's single regeneration with before/after numbers in the commit; if a cell drifts past 5pp that is the finding, stated, not a reason to soften the effect.

items.remaining_work: Author `rounds 2, every 5` (ship plan §6 #55's recommendation) so the fixate is a window and the tank gets the boss back; pin it in the E4 golden (SIM-16, W8-SIM-BALANCE). `sim/model/Encounter.gd`'s validator gains the rule that an M08 `rounds` must be strictly less than its `every` (an authoring error, not a sim case).
items.risk: The validator rule is the part worth keeping: without it the next tier's author tiles the window again and nothing says so.
